articleTitle: Using Machine Learning to Enhance Personalization in E-Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Numerous diverse learning materials can be found on e-learning sites. Students in today's e-learning platforms invest a lot of time and energy in locating pertinent learning materials. The student's actual requirements must be taken into account based on a variety of characteristics, including choices, expertise, and learning style. Education must be pertinent to the necessary concept's environment. This study aims to develop an efficient approach for detecting e-learning style and then customizing the e-learning contents to match that style, using machine learning (ML) algorithms to enhance personalization in e-learning. The blended ensemble method combined with the XGBoost meta-learning approach produced the most prominent results for enhancing e-learning style, with an accuracy of 97.6%. Further, the textual material of the e-files is altered using various natural language processing (NLP) approaches. The spaCy NLP-oriented labeled entity identification (LEI) algorithm achieves a 94.2% F1 value and a 0.92 precise match ratio while color-coded textual production of 10 e-files with 790 different phrases. These alterations are intended to suit students' tastes, resulting in an additional personalized and interactive teaching encounter.

articleTitle: Quantifying Performance Trade-offs in Network Virtualization for Cloud Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Designing a cloud computing environment is a tradeoff performance between costs and way of providing services that System of virtualized networks may affect it. In order to alleviate this, abstractions have to be developed to quantitively measure and decide data plane abstraction performance costs in the cloud computing spaces. Here we provide a technical summary of the work that was aimed at quantifying performance tradeoffs in cloud computing settings from the angle of network virtualization. This study will consider the performance of two such important factors like network latency and resource utilization. Network latency: This is defined as the time taken for a given network packet to travel from a given source to the given destination. Resource utilization, on the other hand, refers to the amount of network resource that used, e.g. how much bandwidth or computational power is used. This will then be supplemented by control the experiment to perform simulations for understanding network configuration effects and simulation threats. This will help in keeping a picture of how these trade-offs affect the overall performance in network virtualization. This study's findings will help network and cloud computing architects in optimizing their networks and alleviating the performance penalties of virtualization. Consequently, this helps in reducing costs and enhancing performance in cloud computing environments.

articleTitle: Integrating Random Forest and XGBoost For Accurate House Rent Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Predicting house rents accurately is essential for tenants, landlords, and investors to make informed decisions in the real estate market, particularly given the rising trends in rental prices. This study employs machine learning techniques, including Random Forest and XGBoost, to predict rental values based on factors such as location, area, square footage, rent, and house size. The dataset was preprocessed using Python libraries such as NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn, with steps including data cleaning, normalization, and feature engineering. Features such as house age, floor details, and distance from city centers were derived to enhance model performance. Evaluation metrics like Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) were used to measure accuracy. The Random Forest algorithm achieved superior results with its robustness against overfitting and its ability to model complex relationships. XGBoost, with its scalability and speed, also delivered competitive performance. The ensemble approach of these models further improved prediction accuracy by leveraging their individual strengths.The developed system achieved exceptional performance metrics, including a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0001, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.01, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.01, and an R-squared value (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) of 0.9998, indicating high accuracy and robustness in predicting house prices This research highlights the utility of advanced machine learning algorithms and proper preprocessing techniques in real estate analytics.

articleTitle: Optimizing Kidney Stone Detection with Vision Transformers and CNNs: A Transfer Learning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Kidney stones are a common and impactful urological condition, with timely and accurate diagnosis being critical to prevent complications such as renal damage and avoid invasive treatments. This study explores the use of advanced deep learning models, including Vision Transformers (ViT), Swin Transformer and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)—specifically XResNet-50, VGG-16, MobileNetV2 and AlexNet—to enhance kidney stone detection from CT scan images. Leveraging a robust dataset of annotated CT scans in JPG format, the approach employs transfer learning which leverages features learnt from the ImageNet dataset to optimize model performance, focusing on classifying cases as either "Kidney Stone Present" or "Kidney Stone Absent". To further improve diagnostic reliability, the Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) identifies and localizes kidney stones within CT images, enhancing understanding of the model’s decision-making and supporting interpretability. Addressing challenges related to dataset imbalance, model interpretability, and generalizability across healthcare settings. By refining these models for kidney stone detection, the main objective of this work is to build a reliable diagnostic tool that aids in clinical judgement and treatment planning, ultimately enhancing patient outcomes and encouraging broader clinical adoption.

articleTitle: Network Security Threats and Mitigation Strategies in Mobile Networks: A Machine Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Mobile phones are integral to our lives and provide a gateway for our communication and online services through mobile networks across the globe. But now mobile networks are becoming more and more woven into the fabric of everyday life, and the risk of mobile security breaches has soared. From data breaches to malware attacks, we are all at the risk of losing money and the data of most people and organizations. To counter to these security threats a variety of classic solutions have been used in sequence such as firewalls and encryption. But the increasing sophistication of threats has rendered more and more of these alternatives impractical. Well, that is where machine learning (ML) techniques come into play. Although AWS security services are not directly related to ML, it can help analyze large amounts of data and identify trends, which can detect and prevent any potential attacks in advance. Thus, our research work encourages the use of ML techniques for detecting and mitigating threats in network security applied in mobile networks. Next, we will gather and evaluate the network traffic information and teach the ML model to identify the malware patterns and anomalies. You are using that model to predict and stop threats in real-time. Finally, we will discuss how ML-based approaches can be used to dynamically adjust security policies and manage resources in mobile networks. This method aims to enhance the overall security of mobile networks by detecting and preventing potential security threats. This will not only stop potential attacks but will also reduce the time and the resources needed for incident response. We hope to further secure and refine the integrity of every aspect of the mobile network ecosystem through this research.

articleTitle: Blockchain for Machine Learning: Security and Trust in Data Sharing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Data security has become the most important things in this current digitalized environment. As in this era, each process leaves a digital footprint and it requires significant monitoring to maintain trust of stakeholders. It necessitates the companies to evaluate their necessary information including the sensitive and confidential data as per their requirements while maintaining data security and customers’ trustworthiness. While managing data security, companies require limited accessibility of their confidential business information. Personal and private information are the most commonly targeted dataset for hackers in this technological age. Since ML is efficient in evaluating huge datasets, companies must prioritize the potential security concerns. To use artificial intelligence (AI) and ML-driven technologies widely, blockchain has become significant to develop faith among the stakeholders. The research evaluates the efficiency of blockchain technology in improving data security while suggesting its integration with ML-based business approaches.

articleTitle: Using Machine Learning to Enhance Cybersecurity Threat Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In cybersecurity, machine learning is becoming more and more significant. Making threat detection more actionable, scalable, and efficient than using conventional methods that call for human intervention is the main goal of using machine learning in cybersecurity. Cybersecurity machine learning issues require efficient, systematic, and theoretical solutions. The subtleties of applying machine learning algorithms to lower cybersecurity threats are examined in this study. The rapid increase of data in cyberspace and the level of precision of attacks necessitate a proactive approach to security. The adversarial nature of online attacks, data quality, and model robustness are some of the subjects covered in this paper. In the context of cybersecurity, ethical issues are also covered, as is the requirement for accountable and transparent AI systems. Through a careful examination of current research and practical implementations, this research demonstrates the vast potential of machine learning (ML) in bolstering cybersecurity defenses. It shows the importance of a well-coordinated approach that combines human expertise with machine learning capabilities. As the environment of cyber threats evolves, organisations seeking to safeguard their data and digital assets must leverage ML's capabilities.

articleTitle: Empowering Social Sciences with Data Visualization - An Insights and Explorations into Behavioral Patterns and Urban Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Visual data is an integral and essential aspect of any science, a powerful tool for description and exploration in social sciences005. Abstract: In this study, we apply new advanced ways of visualization to bring light on steps helping policy makers better understand multifaceted social phenomena using datasets publicly available. Through combining geospatial, temporal and network visualizations, the framework provides an intimate understanding of urban growth patterns of i-Social networks and behavior characteristics. Findings show that attractive visualizations make interpreting and revealing otherwise hidden patterns easier and provide insight into policy. Such an approach would finally close the gap between data complexity and actionable insights, offering social scientists a solid foundation for research with real impact.

articleTitle: Implementation of Adaptive Traffic Inundation Detection Technique in RPL-Based IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Recently, the Internet of Things (IoT) technology facilitates reliable communication for several mission-critical applications. These applications require secure as well as consistent data transmission. However, the Traffic Inundation (TI) attack occupies an internal intrusion device which disseminates misinterpreted data to instigate unnecessary transmissions of the Destination Information Object (DIO) control packets. This damage makes the network incompatible and intensifies a message overhead problem. To mitigate this, a new Adaptive Traffic Inundation Detection (ATID) technique is proposed for Low power and Lossy Networks (LLN). The suggested ATID modifies the traditional Routing protocol for Low Power and Lossy Networks (RPL) function to establish robust verification of new updates. After receiving any updates, the proposed ATID shifted to a legitimacy check phase in order to conclude how to interpret the new updates. Once the TI attacks are identified, it shifts to the attack mitigation phase. By involving these two phases, the proposed ATID achieves maximum detection accuracy rate of 98.6%.

articleTitle: Detecting Bots in Misinformation Campaigns: Strategies and Societal Implications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has reshaped how information is disseminated, with social media platforms emerging as primary sources for news and public discourse. However, this shift has also introduced a new challenge: the widespread spread of misinformation. Bots—automated accounts designed to mimic human behavior—have become key agents in the amplification of misinformation, capable of influencing public opinion on a massive scale. This study explores the role of bots in promoting misinformation, particularly during crucial events like elections, public health crises, and social movements. By adopting a mixed-methods approach that combines behavioral analysis, network traffic monitoring, and natural language processing (NLP), we investigate how bots infiltrate social media platforms, propagate false narratives, and manipulate user behavior. The findings illustrate the growing sophistication of bot networks, the strategies employed to circumvent detection, and the vulnerabilities of social media algorithms that bots exploit. Furthermore, we present an integrated detection framework that leverages machine learning and NLP techniques to identify and mitigate bot-driven misinformation. Our research includes real-world case studies and performance metrics, which demonstrate the framework's effectiveness in reducing the spread of misinformation by up to 30%, while also increasing public awareness. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to combat digital manipulation and preserve the integrity of online information ecosystems.

articleTitle: Nutrient Recycling and Resource Optimization in IoT Based Integrated Poultry and Farming Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: As the global population remain to grow at unprecedented rates, with kingdom turn scarcer for farming intent, creative solutions are required. articleTitle: Challenges and Opportunities in Deploying Explainable AI for Financial Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been used more and more in financial decision-making recently, raising questions about the accountability and transparency of these complex systems. The current study investigates the way Explained Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods might alleviate these concerns and improve the openness of financial decision-making procedures. Nowadays machine learning algorithms are easier to use than ever before, but creating and deploying systems that facilitate real-world banking services has proved challenging. This is mostly due to the fact that algorithms for machine learning are neither transparent or explainable, two attributes that are essential to creating reliable technology. What sets this study unique is the construction of an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that addresses these accessibility concerns while also serving as an instrument for the establishment of credit risk control policies. This work proposes an explainable artificial intelligence model for financing risk control to measure the risks associated with credit financing via peer-to-peer financing networks. The framework uses Shapley parameters to provide AI forecasts according to significant factors that explain. The Support Vector Machine (SVM) and gradient boosting methods had the greatest accuracy scores, 92.4 and 97.6, accordingly. The accuracy of the model was evaluated on a bigger database, and the findings demonstrated that it regularly achieved high levels of accuracy. The SVM and GBM models achieved accuracies of 94.8 and 97.6, respectively.

articleTitle: Diagnosis, Prediction, and Risk Factor Analysis of Multiple Sclerosis Disease using Quantum Machine Learning Classifier
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a condition that affects the brain or central nervous system, which can result in issues with the optic nerve, brain, and spinal cord. Multiple sclerosis is thought to affect 2.8 million people. This research focuses on the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis using Quantum machine learning (QML) classifiers. Several models have been created utilizing various data sets, such as clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data. The quantum machine learning has emerged by the merging of classical machine learning and quantum information processing as a result of the superiority and advancement of quantum computing in various fields (such as encryption, machine learning, and healthcare). The experimental results present a comparative analysis of classical machine learning and quantum machine learning algorithms for the problem under consideration.

articleTitle: DenseNet-Based Approach for Early Detection and Classification of Alzheimer's Disease Using MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Management and treatment of Alzheimer's disease depend on accurate diagnosis and prognosis for the condition. Using a reliable convolutional network, a DenseNet model, this work thoroughly assesses the classification of Alzheimer's disease with the help of MRI data. The suggested method precisely detects and labels several phases of Alzheimer's from MRI scans by using DenseNet depth and feature extraction. This study thoroughly evaluates the proposed model's performance using a dataset of MRI scans of preprocessed and labeled healthy controls, MCI, and AD patients. Regularization methods and transfer learning helped retrain the pre-trained DenseNet model for the medical application using the classification abilities for the right identification. Moreover, the DenseNet model attained a mean test accuracy of 92.5% with skilled data augmentation and model training methods. So, the proposed DenseNet model is. Model complexity and test accuracy are suitable for clinical purposes. These outcomes suggest that DenseNet might work as a tool to support medical diagnosis. Future research will focus on improving the predictive power of the model and investigating its integration into formal clinical processes and decision support systems to improve patient care and raise the science of imaging-based diagnostics of neurological diseases.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach for Poultry Disease Classification and Early Detection: ResNet18
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Essential for world agriculture, chicken production provides the required proteins from eggs and meat. On the other hand, diseases such as Salmonella, New Castle Disease, and Coccidiosis substantially compromise poultry health and result in significant financial losses as well as threatened food supply. Both good treatment and prevention depend on early, precise detection of illnesses. Four classrooms teach the model: Healthy, Coccidiosis, New Castle Disease, and Salmonella to categorise chicken images. Using a 510,000-picture Kaggle dataset 400,000 for training, 40,000 for validation, and 70,000 for testing the ResNet18 model obtained an outstanding general accuracy of 96%. Powerful performance employing routinely accurate projections and powerful generalising to fresh data is shown. By automating this process, this work highlights how well the ResNet18 model detects poultry diseases, therefore assisting in preventing disease in chicken husbandry. The results show how effectively deep learning techniques may enhance poultry health monitoring and food security assurance.

articleTitle: Data Protection and Privacy in HRM: Challenges and Solutions with Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Blockchain innovation offers a protected, decentralized stage for sharing and putting away representative information, which can be utilized to further develop information security in HRM. In spite of the fact that it isn't quite as direct or reliable as the customary methodology, HR generally demands input on the candidate's presentation surveys from his past business. The exhibition evaluation is one approach to inspect and survey a representative's work execution purposefully. This strategy could be exceptionally helpful to an association's HR division. Here, it'll inspect how a blockchain-based framework was utilized to survey a previous representative's presentation.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Image Generation Models: Methods, Comparative Insights, and Available Datasets
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: An era of notable advances in image generation mostly through text-to-image models has been brought about by the development of generative artificial intelligence. Generative AI is a cutting-edge platform. AI models like GAN and DALL E most commonly use in image generation. These technologies help professionals and non-professionals create high-quality, context-relevant digital representations of historical artifacts. This study examines the artificial intelligence role in text-to-image models. We provide a thorough summary of the literature in this field, classifying different types of image generation models. Comparative analysis of previous work done. Along with publicly available datasets.

articleTitle: Proposal and Implementation of Neural Network-Based Approach for Secure Speaker Recognition Using Spectrograms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In this era of Artificial Intelligence, research on Speaker Recognition systems has taken the forefront. In this paper, an efficient deep learning pipeline has been proposed. A total of 7500 audio samples from Kaggle’s speaker recognition dataset have been used to generate Spectrograms, Mel Spectrograms, and Mel-Frequency Cepstrum Coefficients (MFCC), which in turn have been used to train a ResNet 18 Deep Neural Network from scratch. Using different regularization techniques such as dropout, early stopping, and weight decay, high accuracies were obtained. The results generated from the ResNet by using Mel spectrograms, classic spectrograms, and MFCCs were compared alongside each other to check which one among them gave the best testing accuracy. The proposed approach is designed and implemented with additional feature enhanced by providing a secure feature selection system from audio signals. To implement this, the proposed system is equipped with AES security algorithm on splitting of data set into ratio of 60:30:10. The Classic Spectrograms predicted the speakers with 92.96% accuracy. Mel Spectrograms were comparatively more efficient with 93.75% testing accuracy. The results obtained from the model trained with the MFCC features were the best of all, at 95.2%. Further, the usage of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm has also been proposed for a secure speaker recognition task.

articleTitle: Social Media Sentiment as an Indicator of Electoral Outcomes: A Study of Indian General Elections
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The volatile nature of public opinion, increasingly driven by social media platforms such as Twitter, has emerged as a pivotal factor in electoral dynamics. This study targets the 2019 and 2024 Indian general elections, which featured prominent political figures Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi, to quantitatively assess public sentiment through advanced sentiment analysis techniques applied to Twitter data. Utilizing comprehensive datasets from these electoral periods, sentiment polarity was systematically analyzed using the Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) and the VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner) model. Sentiments were classified into positive, negative, and neutral categories, serving as predictors for election outcomes. This approach integrates sentiment scores with machine learning algorithms to model and predict electoral results. The study highlights the efficacy of social media analytics in capturing real-time public opinion, reinforcing the critical role of sentiment analysis and opinion mining in modern electoral studies. The findings provide a robust framework for understanding the influence of digital public sentiment on election outcomes, offering methodological advancements in the predictive modeling of electoral behavior.

articleTitle: Automated Classification of Fresh and Rotten Fruits Using ResNet50 for Enhanced Food Quality Control and Waste Reduction1
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Effective classification of fresh and rotting fruits is essential in the agricultural and food industries for food safety, quality control, and waste minimising purposes. The ResNet50 convolutional neural network (CNN) model is investigated in this work to automatically classify fruit freshness, therefore tackling the difficulty of differentiating between fresh and rotting fruits. Comprising 1,655 images from six categories fresh peaches, fresh pomegranates, fresh strawberries, rotten peaches, rotten pomegranates, and rotten strawberries the ResNet50 model achieves an overall accuracy of 95%. Strong performance across various metrics including precision, recall, and F1-score is shown by the model, which distinguishes fresh pomegranates and rotten strawberries especially with very great accuracy. Training and validation trials show strong generalization with low overfitting; the confusion matrix points up areas needing work and shows how well the model can fairly classify fruits. Emphasizing the ability of automated fruit classifying systems in improving supply chain efficiency and lowering food waste, this work offers a scalable way for fruit quality monitoring.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Open-Source LLMs for Text-to-SQL Conversion in Healthcare Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Large amounts of patient data are stored in Electronic Medical Records (EMR), however querying these databases is complex, and often requires specialized training that medical professionals typically do not have. Data retrieval in this manner can be inefficient, and can delay clinical decision making and impact patient outcomes. Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) demonstrate promising results in natural language processing tasks, but there are few comprehensive studies on the comparison of their effectiveness on text to SQL applications in the healthcare domain. To fill this gap, we compare a wide range of open source LLMs for text to SQL tasks in healthcare based on the MIMICSQL dataset, which is based on the MIMIC-III database, a large, single center dataset with rich critical care patient records. In particular, we evaluated the performance of several open source models, including Llama3.1-8B, Llama3.1 70B, Mixtral-8x7b, Gemma2-9b, and Gemma2-2b, and found that the Llama3.1-70B model performed best at generating correct SQL queries in terms of exact match and logic form accuracy. To support the selection of LLMs for clinical decision support systems, this work identifies models that facilitate access to critical patient information.

articleTitle: AI in Social Media Marketing: Using Machine Learning to Analyze Trends and Predict Consumer Sentiment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Social media marketing (SMM) is prominent in the society at present. Individuals use social networking sites to buy different items. The rapid rise of social networking sites has rendered them essential tools for evaluating consumer sentiments and forecasting a wide range of societal and economic patterns. This study gathered statistics from a variety of social media channels. This study examined data to anticipate user activity on social networking sites. This study took into account user statistics from Twitter, LinkedIn, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and Pinterest, among other platforms. Because social media networks provide a wide range of statistics at elevated speeds and volumes, predicted big data techniques were applied in this study. This investigation studied user conduct on social networking sites using specific metrics and variables. This study examined user perception and attitudes towards social networking platforms. This study preprocessed data to remove outliers, disturbances, errors, and duplicate records, resulting in high-quality results. As a result, in this paper, an integrated system combining sentiment evaluation and machine learning (ML) methods is constructed. This study utilized computational models and ML to anticipate user conduct on social networking platforms. The framework predicts user conduct on social networking platforms. Eighty percent of data has been employed for training, with twenty percent for testing. After testing many conventional and ensemble ML classifiers, decision trees outscored every other method.

articleTitle: SMS Spam Detection using Advance Naive-Bayes Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Recently, with increased use of mobile phones, it has transformed into a multibillion-dollar Short Message Service or SMS. However, the drop in the cost of messaging services has led to an increased number of unsolicited commercial messages, or spam, being delivered to mobile phones. Several reasons exist for which traditional algorithms used in email filtering may not efficiently classify the spam in SMS such as the absence of strong SMS spam databases, with the short length and features of the message, the informal language used, etc. This paper uses a real SMS spam database After preprocessing the data and extraction of relevant features, Naïve Bayes machine learning techniques is applied to get the results. Then it is analyzed using confusion matrix, accuracy, precision and recall values. A learning curve with clearly defined relationship between the training and testing data set and overall error at the end.

articleTitle: Design of Multilayer PCB With SMD Components for Enhanced RFID-Based Security in Pervasive Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This research presents the design and implementation of a smart parking management system utilizing ESP32-CAM modules, RFID technology, and GSM communication. The system automates the vehicle entry process in a parking facility, providing a seamless and efficient experience for users. When a vehicle arrives at the parking entrance, the driver taps an RFID card, which triggers the system to prompt for additional information, such as the driver’s mobile number and name. The system then captures images of both the driver and the vehicle using two ESP32-CAM modules and stores this data along with a unique registration code on the RFID card. Bluetooth communication between the ESP32-CAM modules ensures that the process of capturing images is efficient and synchronized. The SIM800L GSM module sends an SMS to the driver containing details such as the vehicle’s entry time, charges based on the duration of stay, and links to the captured images. The integration of an OLED display, a physical keyboard, and a buzzer provides user feedback and enhances the overall usability of the system. The research demonstrates the potential of combining microcontroller-based systems with IoT technologies to create a practical solution for parking management. The use of RFID for identification, Bluetooth for inter-device communication, and GSM for real-time updates ensures a comprehensive and user-friendly approach to parking management. This system can be deployed in various environments, offering an effective method for improving the efficiency and security of parking operations.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Location-Based XML Indexing in Real-Time Wireless Data Broadcasting for IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is fast revolutionizing a number of sectors by performing real-time data collection and analysis. Effective data broadcasting protocols become increasingly important as IoT devices. Specifically designed for Internet of Things applications, this paper proposes a comprehensive framework for location-based XML indexing in real-time wireless data broadcasting. To enable effective geographic-based XML data searching, we propose a spatial XML indexing technique. Our proposed broadcasting strategy maximizes network use also. The suggested solution ensures energy efficiency of various IoT devices while addressing the issues of scalability and changing data environments.

articleTitle: Empowering Senior Health Through Digital Literacy: A Review of Impactful Initiatives
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In recent years, the COVID-19 epidemic, like other worldwide disasters, has profoundly affected elderly people’s daily routines, social networks, and healthcare. years. Although remote healthcare access and decreased isolation are considered advantages of digitalization and automation of services, these technologies There are also learning curves, privacy and security issues and unfamiliarity difficulties. All of these problems ultimately require health informatics, gerontology, social psychology, human–computer interaction, cybersecurity, and privacy disciplines to work together. This paper focuses on the artificial intelligence’s role for digital inclusion, safety and well-being within an aging population in the context of an increasingly digitized ecosystem.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection for Sensor Manipulation in Matter Enabled-IoT Devices with Faulty Data Injection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The security of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in Matter-enabled networks is crucial, as attacks such as sensor spoofing and data injection can lead to significant disruptions. Sensor manipulation attacks where the attackers manipulate the sensor inputs to create erroneous behavior in devices are issues of serious concern for anomaly detections. Faulty sensor data can cause devices to operate in unsafe or inefficient conditions across various applications, compromising system reliability and performance. The Isolation Forest algorithm is employed to isolate faulty data injections as outliers in sensor readings, offering a robust method for anomaly detection. The approach, therefore, focuses on the possibility of enhancing detection with greater reliability in IoT networks. The lightweight and extensible approach also assembles a process of strengthening Matter-based networks against vulnerabilities emanating from wrong control feedback.

articleTitle: hA Hybrid Model Combining Vision Transformer and Generative Pre-trained Transformer for Image Captioning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)

authors.preferredName: Jatangi Y D M V Prasada Vishwesh
authors.firstName: Jatangi Y D M V Prasada

abstract: Creating descriptive captions for images is now becoming a mission-critical application area in the intersection of natural language processing and computer vision. This work provides the hybrid model VisionGPT2, combining Vision Transformer for encoding images and GPT2 for text generation, which enables accurate, coherent, and context-aware image descriptions. The model is tested over a dataset by using BLEU score metrics and has achieved a high BLEU score of 0.4877, which ascertains the strength of cross-modal architectures for image captioning. In this paper, the design and training process of VisionGPT2 has been discussed along with the benefits and challenges faced while proceeding and the potential applications the model has gained in performance for future use.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Intrusion Detection: Navigating Challenges and Embracing AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The emergence of networked autonomous systems has brought a new wave of security threats. Because of not be able to adopt the traditional intrusion detection approaches with the new threats, AIML based cybersecurity defences have gain more attention in recent times. The current state of AIML-based intrusion and abuse detection is examined in this paper, with a focus on significant scientific advancements and the real-world obstacles preventing its broad deployment. As cyberattacks become more sophisticated, one thing has remained the same: Intrusion Detection Systems are a must for protecting digital infrastructures, and they need to be robust. This review summarises the awareness of IDS from traditional signature-based methods to an upcoming disruptive focus on Artificial Intelligence, especially ML and DL. We present a comparison of the advantages and disadvantages of these techniques, emphasizing challenges such as dataset limitations, adaptability to operate in real-time and detecting unseen attacks. Forthcoming, we examine new research directions (hybrid methods, ensemble learning and challenging advanced datasets) to improve the efficacy of IDS on ever more complicated network landscapes.

articleTitle: Exploring the Capabilities and Limitations of Generative AI Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Unprecedented capabilities for content generation, predictive analytics, and automation are made available by the introduction of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies, which uses in a new age of industrial innovation. The purpose of this study is to investigate the transformational potential of generative AI from the perspective of exploring its capabilities and limitations and highlighting its role in the development of future technological developments. With the help of this study, we want to highlight important unsolved issues in contemporary generative AI paradigms. These challenges need to be addressed in order to further improve the capabilities, variety, and dependability of these concepts. Our goal is to give researchers with significant insights that will allow them to explore successful research areas, which will ultimately lead to the creation of generative AI systems that are more robust and accessible.

articleTitle: An Integrated Approach to Altitude Monitoring and Logging for Adventure and Scientific Use with Data Logging with Web Server Monitor
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Wherever people venture, be it in relaxation mode while hiking or gorgeous activities like ballooning or aviation, keeping track of altitude holds immense importance. All of these require the capacity to measure and track how the altitude changes over time in real-time as safety practices, navigation needs, and optimization advantages. Nonetheless, existing altitude tracking technologies usually depend on dedicated approaches or particular systems which are limited and do not provide a wide range of usability. This technology provides an entirely new way of measuring and recording altitude, a method which is cost effective and easy to use and incorporates state of the art technology to improve the quality of data. This system does not indicate the necessity and dependency of any external communication networks as the system can be used within the region or other geographical area where the altitude is of course important. When altitude is to be monitored the system is self-sufficient in that it stores altitude parameters while providing data at the same time. This dual integration of data features ensures that information about the recent activity done by the user as well as records of activities done earlier are presented to online users.In the case of aviation and ballooning operations, where there exists the constant need to manage altitude changes most accurately, having accurate information with respect to the altitude is, in fact, an absolute necessity. In the same way, concerning outdoor leisure activities such as hiking, while helping in navigation, altitude tracking provides useful information regarding climate or physical performance. This new development is, therefore, positioned to evolve from professional systems to more user-friendly systems that log and capture altitude movement data continuously over a period of time allowing expansion in applications. This work explains the need for effective altitude monitoring with regard to safety and recreation aspects. The advancement is beneficial in the monitoring of altitude in that it prevents end users from compromising on safety standards, data quality, and end-user satisfaction among other areas in altitude sensitive activities. The absence of any qualifying requirements with respect to connected external networks only enhances the app's usability in the field since many such circumstances happen outdoors.

articleTitle: Optimization of Wireless Network Performance Through Intelligent Resource Allocation: A Game Theory Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Increasing resources were allocated based on the demand for wireless network services. Game theory has recently been recognized as a potential solution for enhancing wireless networks by jointly optimizing resource allocation among users. Specifically, a common approach in this direction is to formulate wireless networks as multi-player games in which the users compete with each other for the available resources, e.g., bandwidth, power, time, etc. Applying the principles of game theory can lead to the creation of a Nash equilibrium, such that no one player can better their results if they change their strategy independently. Game-theoretic-based intelligent Resource Allocation Algorithms Enable This Type of Equilibrium, Whereby Users Employ Negotiation and Cooperation, Therefore Allocating Network Resources Efficiently and Achieving Higher Performance. A game theory approach for wireless network optimization: A technical paper By considering the changing network conditions along with user preferences, an efficient resource allocation method has been proposed. To do this, it intelligently schedules user transmissions, minimizing interference and maximizing throughput. Simulation results and experiments in the real world demonstrate that the game-theory unstable approach improves the performance of wireless networks over resource allocation based on classical methods. Furthermore, due to being scalable, robust, and resource-efficient, our approach can be deployed in different large-scale wireless networks. A part of this work is to implement smart allocation schemes of resource for wireless networks that will help to enhance more reliable and efficient wireless services in future.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of Network Protocols for Mobile Ad-hoc Networks with Non-Ideal Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Mobile ad-hoc networks (MANETs) have attracted a lot of interest unpaid to their low cost, give, and ease of distribution in many scenarios. Unfortunately, many of these challenges arise because it is deployed in environments that are made non-ideal due to interference, node mobility, and limited resources. In a self-configuring type of network, no infrastructure is required to enable communication. Hence, the role of network protocols is critical in a MANET to ensure effective communication and resource utilization. This work attempts to design a universal model that helps in analyzing the performance of network protocols in an environment that holds non-ideal conditions in MANETs. Various parameters like node mobility, interference and resource constraints from real-world scenarios will be included in the model. We will also look at multiple network protocols, such as routing, congestion control, and quality of service protocols. A pseudo-research method that [uses a mixture of simulation and mathematical modelling techniques] will be used to examine the performance of the various protocols under a range of non-ideal scenarios. In this way, one of the objectives of this study is to recognize the advantages and drawbacks of existing protocols and monitor the progress of new protocols created thusly of MANETs that practice in non-ideal conditions.

articleTitle: A Framework for Evaluating the Effectiveness of Explainability Methods in Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a new framework that is transforming societies across the globe into smart towns. Nevertheless, because of IoT systems' ongoing connection and data exchange, their rise has been followed by several cybersecurity problems. In response to this issue, several intrusion detection structures (IDSs) have been developed as safety precautions. These methods have shown effectiveness in thwarting several IoT-based assaults, particularly when deep learning (DL) techniques are employed. While there is a lot to discuss on the topic of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) nowadays, more research is still required to completely comprehend how effective XAI is at identifying assault areas and routes when implemented in cyber safety uses. This research provides an innovative, explainable IDS for IoT systems. This study designed an IDS utilizing a Short-Term Long Memory (LSTM) framework to detect intrusions and analyze the system's choices. For training and assessing the LSTM algorithm, an innovative collection of source characteristics is gathered using a new SPIP (S- Shapley Addition ExPlanations, P- Permuting Characteristic Significance, I- Individual Conditioned Expectations, P- Partial Dependent Graph) architecture. When contrasted with existing competitor approaches, the SPIP architecture outperformed them in terms of identification accuracy, processing duration, and comprehension of data characteristics and models. The suggested method could help managers and decision-makers comprehend complicated assault activity.

articleTitle: Unmasking Image Authenticity: Classifying Real and Fake Human Faces Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Advancement of deepfake technology and its misuse has become a challenge. This study focuses on the detection of AI-generated fake human face pictures which is proven to be a critical task. For maintaining trust in digital media, encouraging responsible consumption and production, protecting personal data, and to prevent the spread of misinformation, the efficient detection of fake pictures is important. To classify synthetic and real pictures, CNN model was employed to address this challenging issue. There was total 10,000 pictures in the data collection which was further split into 2 categories - 3000 pictures for validation phase and 7000 pictures for training phase. The CNN architecture was trained to classify synthetic and real pictures with subtle differences in visual features. With an 89% classification accuracy, the model shows potential for practical uses in cases when exact identification of bogus images is absolutely required. This result highlights how well CNNs perform in the field of photo classification, particularly in recognizing deepfake content, thereby supporting peace, justice, and robust institutions as well as innovation and infrastructure.

Author Keywords: Real – Fake Face Image Detection Model

articleTitle: Efficient HyperFused Model for Stratification of Concurrent Facial Expressions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This article represents a novel method called HyperFusion that amalgamates Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with Support Vector Machines (SVM) to enhance classification precision and computational competence in facial expression recognition which involves high-dimensional datasets. HyperFusion leverages PCA for dimensionality reduction by extracting the most significant features in stratifying the concurrent facial expressions, while discarding irrelevant or redundant data. This reduction streamlines the feature space, making the SVM classifier more effective by mitigating the curse of dimensionality and improving generalization. SVM then classifies the data using an optimal hyperplane in the lower-dimensional subspace generated by PCA. The fusion of these two methods results in faster training times, reduced complexity, and improved classification accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that HyperFusion achieves an outstanding performance concerning accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional SVM classifiers applied to untransformed high-dimensional data. The proposed method HyperFusion produces 90.3 % accuracy for CK+ dataset. This approach is particularly well-suited for tasks involving large feature sets, noisy data, and applications where real-time processing is critical.

articleTitle: Exploring Emerging AI and IoT Technologies to Enhance Customer Relationship Management in 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence, Internet of Things for management of 5G networks to revolutionize customer relationship management. It enables customer engagement, efficiency and levels of personalization. The study explores the emergence of IoT and AI to enhance CRM framework within low-latency and high-speed infrastructure provided using 5G technology. Real time data collection with IoT and AI driven data analytics that offer actionable insights to enable customer behaviour, enabling adaptive and predictive CRM strategies. Additionally, enhanced connectivity with 5G technology to facilitate integration of smart devices to ensure interactive and consistent experience for the customers. The present study examined the operational and technical synergy between the technologies and has high impact on the efficiency of CRM, implementation challenges that include data security and privacy concerns.

articleTitle: Combining Convolutional Neural Networks with Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Robotics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in robotics, particularly in the advancement of gaming robotics, has drawn a lot of interest as technological and scientific developments continue to advance. This innovation opens up new possibilities for creating smart autonomous robots for gaming. Nevertheless, there is more work to be done to achieve great accuracy and consistency in motion management. The challenges of the robotics' level of smart and the motion-capturing structure's capacity to prevent interruption still require resolution, although numerous methods have been put out to improve monitoring accuracy by merging various data. This study proposes an adaptable reinforcement learning (RL)-oriented multifaceted data combination (AdRL-MDC) system for training a robotic hand to play games alongside humans. It incorporates an adaptable training process for updating the ensemble classification algorithm, an RL paradigm that provides the robots with smart knowledge, and a multifaceted data combination framework that is resistant to interruption. The following studies demonstrate the AdRL-MDC system's previously indicated functionality. The ensemble framework, which combines a convolutional neural network (CNN), performs well in terms of accuracy and computing duration. Furthermore, the depth vision-oriented CNN classification algorithm achieves one hundred percent recognition accuracy, implying that the forecasted motions are the real value.

articleTitle: A Multi-Criteria Decision Making Approach for E-Commerce: An Evolutionary Study with Spring Boot Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The lockdown period witnessed a significant boom in Electronic Commerce (E-Commerce) websites, enabling people to make purchases safely and securely from their homes. A substantial portion of the population now relies on this industry, particularly in the B2C (Business-to-Customer) segment, where businesses operate online and offer direct services to customers. This study explores the integration of multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methodologies to provide customers with diverse product options and sufficient time to make informed purchasing decisions. The implementation employs React.js for frontend development, Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) for design enhancement, Java Spring Boot for backend development, and MySQL for database management.

articleTitle: Gesture to Speech: Deep Learning Models for Real-Time Sign Language Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This study looks into the application of a YOLOv5s model for real-time detection and interpretation of sign language. This is a significant improvement which will help the deaf and hard of hearing communicate more easily. Progress is being made in sign language detection, there are still potential to improve with the accuracy. Through a critical analysis of current methodologies, this research identifies shortcomings in existing models, such as insufficient generalization across different sign languages and real-time performance problems. The proposed work aims to close these gaps by utilizing the effectiveness of YOLOv5s, optimizing hyperparameters, and incorporating transfer learning techniques to increase accuracy and resilience. The results are intended to make sign language recognition systems more inclusive, flexible, and effective, encouraging increased accessibility in communication technology.

articleTitle: Future Trends in HRM: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Automation in Shaping the Workplace
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence-based applications are integrated in the human resource management of firms for managing people within the region as well as international organisations. In the past years the growth of AI based applications proliferates the function of HR M that triggers to exciting new stream to study the effect of AI adoption on business level and individual outcomes. It evaluates the AI enabled HRM practises. The technology examines the firms with problem solving, decision making and utilisation of resources and opportunities for employees. The growing interest on AI based technologies for HRM for diffusion of innovation in large multinational enterprises. AI has the capability for reduction of administrative burden experienced by the HR Professional that allows them for precise decision making based on the data patterns. Adoption of artificial intelligence helps in effective employee management and decision making. So that employee of HR management can overcome the challenges. The study aims to analyse the future trends in HRM and the role of artificial intelligence and automation in shaping the workplace.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of Cross-Layer Optimization scheme for Wireless Mesh Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Mesh wireless networks have significant promise for providing wireless connections in vast and dynamic routes. On the other hand, their performance is hindered by interference, congestion, and unstable connectivity. To resolve these difficulties, several different cross-layer optimization strategies have been presented to ease inter-layer communication and maximize the network's overall performance. This research evaluates the effectiveness of CLO schemes in WMNs from a performance standpoint. By conducting simulation-based tests and doing a comprehensive literature analysis, we were able to determine the efficacy of CLO in terms of throughput, latency, and packet loss. System Cluster, Distributed Cloud, Load Balancing, and Cloud-based Load Balancing are all similar terms. When combined with a mechanism that allows for coordination across layers, CLO methods will enhance network resource management, reducing the likelihood of collisions and congestion in wireless mesh networks (WMNs). This evaluation reveals how the performance of WMNs may be improved by using CLO schemes and how feasible it is to put these schemes into reality. This study's findings may assist in designing and deploying wireless mesh networks that are both efficient and trustworthy. This is because the demand for wireless connections is growing.

articleTitle: IoT-Propelled Sustainable Aquaponics System for Enhanced Efficiency and Reliability
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The UN has declared sustainability as the main theme for the world for 21st century. As per the UN designed 17 SDGs, the SDG-2 (Zero Hunger) mainly focuses a sustainable food source for world population. According to report of FAO in 2021, the food consumption was 2.5 million metric tonnes and will rise by 35% in 2030. Traditional methods are not enough for this, thus innovative food production technique needs to be implemented in order to accomplish the goal. In such desperate times, Aquaponics has resulted as a developing cuisine yielding technology holding the potential to yield this output rate but even this domain requires further advancements to reduce efforts. Thus IoT, an emerging technology, is integrated in the framework of aquaculture to advance it. An IoT based smart aquaponics arrangement is implemented to supervise and alter water quality constraints including pH, temperature, oxygen rate, nitrate, ammonium, electric conduction, etc in a water tank or body. Furthermore, visual devices are used to capture fishes and plants on a consistent origin to display their healthiness or presence of disease among them using images. These images are enhanced with various techniques such as Image preprocessing, segmentation, etc to achieve higher accuracy. The study concludes that there are still some aspects which can progress such as the unexplored parameters that contribute to water quality and disease management among the school of fishes.

articleTitle: Stress reduction through Music using ESP8266
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This paper aims to reduce stress through music therapy using ESP8266 microcontroller. The system monitors physiological signals like skin conductance and heart rate to select calming music in real-time. Techniques such as rhythmic entrainment, guided relaxation music, and binaural beats are applied. Among these, rhythmic entrainment proved the most effective in promoting relaxation. This wearable, cost-effective solution offers personalized stress relief through music.

articleTitle: Real-Time Gaze Tracking for Online Examination
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The exponential growth in online education has increased the demand for automated systems to ensure academic integrity during online examinations. A real-time proctoring system addresses this need by monitoring a student's eye gaze and head movements during an exam. This system leverages Dlib's pre-trained frontal face detector and 68-point facial landmark predictor to detect facial features and track the direction of eye movement and head position. By analyzing these metrics, the system can flag behaviors associated with potential cheating, such as looking away from the screen for extended periods. This paper discusses the design and implementation of the proctoring system, details the detection algorithms, and evaluates its effectiveness for real-time monitoring.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of VGG16, InceptionV3 and ResNet50 for Lung Cancer Detection in Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Lung cancer is among the primary reasons of cancer-related fatalities. Globally, that underscoring urgent need for efficient early detection techniques. The aim of this study to estimate and contrast the capabilities of three well-known deep learning architecturesVGG16, InceptionV3 and ResNet for lung cancer detection using CT scans. A comprehensive dataset of annotated lung CT images was utilized to assess each model’s accuracy and loss values. Our findings reveal that in terms of accuracy, compared to the other models, VGG performed better and inference speed, achieving the highest sensitivity and specificity rates. InceptionV3 demonstrated a strong balance between performance and computational demands, while VGG16, though simpler, still provided competitive results. The implication of the research shows that VGG16 may serve as a accurate tool for clinicians, enhancing the accuracy of lung cancer diagnoses and potentially improving outcome of patient. In future, we should focus on integrating these models into clinical workflows and their applications in real-time detection scenarios. The VGG16 model shows highest accuracy for lung cancer detection in between all three models. This result shows accuracy of 71% for lung cancer detection

articleTitle: Comprehensive Framework for Analyzing Grammar Error Correction with GPT -3.5
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This investigate assesses the viability and exactness of an error-correction approach utilizing GPT-3.5 compared to routine instruments. Letter set rectification plays a vital part in making strides the quality of and improving clarity in different scholastic and proficient situations. Be that as it may, it does confront a few challenges, such as affectability to input varieties and intermittent overcorrection. The think about recommends entering on moving forward relevant understanding and diminishing overcorrection to development these calculations assist. It too investigates potential applications of GPT-3.5 for upgrading composing back and languagelearning assets, highlighting conceivable future investigate ranges to optimize AI-driven language structure rectification models.

articleTitle: Elongation of NFT Framework Using ERC721
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) are the most recent trends in owning and trading digital assets. In this paper Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) are secured using cryptography approach ERC721 based on the secure consensus technique that maintains all unit data in a unique identity code that is particular to each digital boon. This technique proposes augmentation in terms of security, transparency, and fractional ownership. However, with the unprecedented prospects for the creative sector and beyond, these markets have the potential to completely transform the digital art and collectibles market. The future scope of proposed technique is to overcome the gaps identified as surrounding sustainability, scalability, user experience, and regulation.

articleTitle: Cooperative Wireless Network Clustering and Routing Using Ant Colony Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The Cooperative Wireless Network Clustering and Routing uses Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) to enhance communication in wireless networks. Ant colony optimization (ACO) is a bio-inspired optimization technique that mimics the way ants search for the shortest distance between their food and home. CWCR is based on homogenous nodes, which simply cluster group nodes and select the cluster heads to manage intra-cluster communication. ACO: It is used to place the cluster head appropriately and to determine the routes that provide efficient data transfer between such cluster heads. Thus, it gives less energy and network cost by less hops & avoiding congested regions. The ACO algorithm further allows for dynamic clustering, which reconfigures the clusters according to the changing concentration of vehicles in the environment. It considers link quality, channel available to nodes and energy levels to decide. Moreover, CWCR performs much better than existing routing algorithms in energy efficiency, throughput and scalability. Flooding can be used in different classes of wireless networks, including sensor networks, ad-hoc networks and cognitive radio networks. CWCR has the potential to greatly improve the performance of wireless networks, and real-world feasible scenarios of its deployment exist.

articleTitle: Customer Experience Management in age of AI: Strategies for Personalization and Loyalty
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Since its birth, a great deal of study has focused on understanding the importance of AI in the business context. Given this, the goal of this study is to assess the effects of AI on client devotion and experiences and how personalisation mediates this relationship. This study had two goals in mind. After examining the various uses of AI in business, we use data from 900 companies worldwide to assess experimentally if these uses boost customer loyalty. The combined scores of four different AI traits make up the datasets: natural language processing integration, AI-powered customer service, predictive modelling, and ML-powered personalisation. The binary customer loyalty measure is the goal. Each component is measured using a 5-point Likert scale. Three different supervised machine learning (ML) techniques were employed: logistic regression, SVM, and decision trees. Confusion matrices were used to assess each algorithm's performance. With a test accuracy of 69.04%, the logistic classifiers outperformed the others. The accuracies of the decision tree and SVC were 64.39 and 58.96, respectively. The results of this study demonstrate how companies can utilise AI, ML, and NLP to analyse data and determine what's valuable. These insights can then be used to automate operations and inform company plans. Therefore, businesses should implement them if they want to stay competitive and boost client loyalty.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Security: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The applications of the Internet of things(IoT) have grown at an exponential rate in recent years. However, it also brings up security-related concerns. While the common response techniques like firewalls, antivirus software, spyware, and authentication mechanisms offer security in many domains, viruses and intrusion attacks continue to pose a threat. To solve this issue, our research performs a thorough comparison of the different machine learning techniques, evaluating how well they can detect and predict attacks associated with the Internet of Things. This article uses Machine learning (ML) algorithms to thoroughly investigate early identification strategies for IoT attacks. We do this by using the UNSW-NB15 Dataset collected from Kaggle. Three machine learning algorithms—Logistic regression (LR), k-nearest neighbors (k-NN), and Gradient boosting (GB) analyzed with the UNSW-NB15 dataset in this research. In order to evaluate how effectively algorithms identify attacks, many performance metrics are used. These metrics include accuracy, recall, F1 score, ROC curve, and confusion matrix. This analysis helps choose the best machine learning methods for a given IoT security scenario. This comparative analysis provides crucial insights to researchers, practitioners, and industry professionals striving to secure IoT ecosystems against expanding cyber threats, laying the foundation for the growth of IoT attack detection approaches.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fetal Health Prediction Using Machine Learning and Ensemble Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The United Nations seeks to diminish preventable deaths by 2030; yet, maternal and child mortality continue to pose significant global health issues. Attaining this objective necessitates fetal health monitoring, and cardiotocography (CTG) data, which records fetal heart rate and uterine contractions, provides a valuable, non-invasive approach to assessing fetal health. In response to the global challenge of child and maternal mortality, which saw over 295,000 maternal fatalities in 2017, this study explored the application of machine learning to enhance fetal health monitoring through Cardiotocography (CTG) data analysis. While CTG provides a non-invasive method for monitoring fetal health, traditional manual analysis is prone to subjectivity and errors, necessitating automated solutions. The research utilized a comprehensive dataset of 2,126 CTG records with 21 features, implementing various machine learning models including Stacked Model, XGBoost, Blended Model, Random Forest, KNN, SVM, and Logistic Regression after preprocessing the data through normalization and validation. The results demonstrated the superior performance of ensemble methods, with the Stacked Model achieving the highest accuracy of 96.00%, followed closely by XGBoost at 95.88%, while traditional models like KNN, SVM, and Logistic Regression showed lower performance ranging from 87.79% to 91.54%. Looking forward, the study suggests several promising directions for advancement, including the integration of deep learning architectures, development of real-time monitoring systems, enhancement of model interpretability through explainable AI, and exploration of personalized medicine applications, all aimed at ultimately reducing maternal and fetal mortality rates through more accurate and timely health assessments in clinical settings

articleTitle: Unique Image Identification and Ownership Monitoring using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Blockchain technology has largely revolutionized modern life. The impact of blockchain with its immutable and irreversible transactions has given rise to many modern technological models, and the same is true for the unique identification of images. Numerous issues related to the unique identification of images and owner tracing like signature verification, secure image transactions and much more, this can be addressed using blockchain. In the present era, it is exceptionally easy to steal or alter digital artwork and photos. This research, which focuses mostly on digital artwork and images, offers promise in addressing issues related to intellectual property rights. The research paper proposes a method for tracking ownership of data and maintaining authentic historic records related to image creation using technologies like blockchain, steganography and digital watermarking. Many models have been proposed to counter the issues related to image owner identification. Blockchain technology is making rapid progress in this field to solve problems and improve existing solutions. By incorporating multiple hashing techniques like Phash, Dhash, and cryptographic hashing and other technologies and concepts like steganography, we aim to establish an efficient system for uniquely identifying images and tracing their owners.

articleTitle: Teaching Machine Learning in K–12 Education: Potential and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)

authors.preferredName: Jhonn Robert Ruiz De La Cruz

abstract: A growing number of from kindergarten to twelve and colleges and universities are using machine learning (ML) methods, which have shown promise in a variety of computer domains. The study needs to comprehend how awareness and freedom are formed in these frameworks. However, one of the challenges facing computer education studies is incorporating artificial intelligence and classical mathematical thinking into the school curriculum. Research on how individuals learn to prepare, evaluate, enhance, and implement machine learning systems is lacking, particularly in the K–12 educational area, despite machine learning's pivotal role in today's technology. This article places current research in the computing learning setting. Outlines variations that K–12 computing instructors should consider when tackling this obstacle, and graphs arising pathways in educational reality, concept, and innovation related to instructing machine learning in schools in grades K–12. To properly include ML in the more comprehensive K–12 computer curriculum, the paper focuses on significant aspects of the perspective shift.

articleTitle: Enhanced Security In Matter-Enabled Iot Networks Through Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The adoption of Matter-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) networks has significantly improved interoperability and security in smart environments. However, despite these advancements, mesh networks within the Matter protocol remain vulnerable to security threats, particularly packet flooding attacks. These attacks generate excessive network traffic, causing packet loss, delays, and overall performance degradation. While Matter includes robust security features such as end-to-end encryption, authentication, and replay protection, these measures are insufficient for detecting flooding attacks in real time.This research proposes an intelligent anomaly detection framework that utilizes telemetry data to identify devices contributing to harmful traffic. By employing the Isolation Forest algorithm, the framework accurately distinguishes abnormal network behaviors—such as increased retry attempts and prolonged message delivery times—from normal operations. Experimental results demonstrate its ability to detect malicious activity with high accuracy and minimal false positives.The study underscores the importance of real-time anomaly detection in protecting Matter IoT networks from flooding attacks. The proposed solution is both scalable and resource-efficient, making it well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained IoT environments.

articleTitle: Automated Fruit Disease Diagnosis Leveraging Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Fruits are some of the most nutrient-dense cash crops that can be found on Earth. Because fruits can vary greatly in size, shape, color, and texture, manually classifying and disease-detecting a big amount of fruit is a time-consuming and error-prone procedure that demands substantial human involvement. As a hybrid ensemble method for identification and classification, this research presents a new multilayer fusion approach that combines rigorous preprocessing, segmentation, and classification of fruit images. Using this method, fruit diseases can be identified and fruits can be categorized. Few data points, different kinds of fruit, different quality standards, and inconsistent disease classifications are some of the problems they found in the existing literature that stem from relying on a single data source. They greatly aggregated and pre-processed multi-fruit data such that the resulting model could be used to large-scale datasets that included both disease recognition and fruit classification. Standard and improved images of a variety of fruits were included in the multi-fruit imagery data set. These included apple, banana, cherry, avocado, grape, blue, guava, mango, pineapple, strawberry, and papaya. Similarly, they standardised the images and built an auto-labeling system using the preexisting picture clusters to reliably place erroneous data into the correct buckets. lastly checked the auto-labeled data for correct class assignment by going over it thoroughly. Python simulations show that the proposed ensemble classifier outperforms all prior methods of fruit categorization and disease identification, with an accuracy of 96.93%.

articleTitle: EfficientNet-B3 for Advanced Insect Classification: Achieving Superior Accuracy in Ten Distinct Classes
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Using deep learning techniques, we provide an advanced insect classification system in this work to classify photos into 10 different classes: Bees, Beetle, Butterflies, Cicada, Dragonflies, Grasshoppers, Moths, Scorpions, Snails, and Spiders.
