Our dataset consists of 10,000 insect photos split into training, validation, and test sets with 8,000, 1,000, and 1,000 images respectively. We used the EfficientNet-B3 transfer learning model, well-known for its dependability and image classification task effectiveness. To learn complex patterns and properties, our data collection helped the architecture to be refined. Our architecture proved to be efficient with an efficacy of 98%. This study shows the opportunities of EfficientNet-B3 in automating and efficient detection of insect classification through amazing accuracy. which also contributes to the domains of entomology and biodiversity. By encouraging innovation in research and development, sustaining life on land through biodiversity preservation, monitoring insect populations to improve climate action, and so strengthening worldwide partnerships for sustainable development, this effort corresponds with the Sustainable Development Goals.

articleTitle: Quantum Linguistics in Patient-Clinical Trial Relations for Improved Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The healthcare industry is undergoing a fundamental revolution with the integration of Quantum Natural Language Processing techniques for matching patient-clinical trials. This research envisions a paradigm where patients and clinical trials collaborate, changing the way healthcare is supplied and medical research is conducted. Apart from this, the research focuses on engaging patients in clinical trials. Patient involvement refers to the process by which patients and their healthcare providers collaborate to make decisions regarding their health. Within the framework of clinical studies, this may entail participants providing input on study designs or monitoring their data through wearable technology and smartphone apps. Quantum NLP has the potential to enhance patient outcomes and advance medical knowledge more quickly by enabling more precise and effective clinical trials. By setting the framework for future applications of quantum NLP, this study expands the conversation on the connection between quantum computing and healthcare.

articleTitle: Enhancement of underwater images using GAN and Refinement network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: A refinement network is a need to further improve the generated images by fine-tuning the output, focusing on enhancing finer details and textures, especially in challenging underwater environments. The enhancement of aquatic visuals is critical challenge in computer vision due to the inherent difficulties posed by low-light conditions and the scattering of light underwater. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhance the quality deep sea images using GAN integrated alongside a refinement network. The proposed method leverages a three-stage architecture consisting of a Generator, Discriminator, and a Refinement Network to deal with the concern of dreadful visibility, color distortion, and low contrast in deep-sea images. The generator is designed to learn the mapping between the degraded input images and their enhanced counterparts through a series of layers, whereas the Discriminator works to differentiate between real and fake (generated) images to guide the generator’s learning process. The model is trained using a custom dataset consisting of paired underwater images and their enhanced versions, with performance evaluated using metrics. The results highlight that the integration of the refinement network considerably improves the visual quality and fidelity of the generated images, outperforming traditional image enhancement methods. Additionally, the model shows robustness in handling varying underwater conditions, making it applicable for real-world applications in marine biology, underwater robotics, and environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Security Vulnerabilities in IPv6 Link-Local Networks: An Examination of DAD Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Computer networking is understanding a network of connected computers that may communicate and share resources, by following a set of principles referred to as communications protocols. The Internet Protocol (IP) lies in the network layer protocol that forms a part of the Internet protocol suite, enabling the transmission of data packets across different network boundaries. To join a network, a device requires an IPv6 address, which must be different and unique. The DAD process is a helpful method for finding duplicate addresses in a network. When a machine enters the network, it must generate a distinct IPv6 address to connect with other nodes Before assigning an IPv6 home address to the physical interface, Duplicate address detection (DAD), an essential technique, assures that it is the only IPv6 home address on the local-area-network (LAN). This paper digs into significance of DAD, its potential vulnerabilities, and various solutions proposed by the authors. Additionally, this paper provides several literary perspectives and recommends potential areas for future research on DAD.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Traditional Medicinal Leaf Recognition and Medical Use Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: An innovative method of conserving and applying traditional knowledge about plants is provided by fusing traditional knowledge of therapeutic plants with contemporary machine learning techniques. In order to create a scalable and user-friendly platform that is accessible through an intuitive interface, this research offers a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based system for the identification of medicinal leaves. The system identifies leaves and offers conventional medicinal information, such as the disease it can cure, uses, dosages, and restrictions, using a dataset of Indian medicinal plants. A Gradio interface is used to create the system, allowing for highly accurate real-time identification. The findings demonstrate how the system unites conventional methods with contemporary technology, offering researchers, medical professionals, and botanists a useful tool.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Fraud Detection in Banking Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Money transfers have significantly increased as a result of the quick development of technological advances, and fraud has also increased in tandem. The overall declines resulting from forged payments worldwide are continuously increasing, according to data on worldwide economic data. The digital transformation of financial interactions will make payment fraud worse by placing more strain on payment providers. Consequently, identifying fraudulent activity has emerged as an intriguing subject. Employing real-world unbalanced databases this study applied a machine learning (ML) oriented system for banking data fraud detection. To fix the problem of the groups not being balanced, the Synthetized Minority over-sampling technology (SMOTE) was employed to resample the database. It was found that the Adaptable Booster (AdaBoost) method worked best with these machine learning techniques when it came to classification. To test the methods, performance matrices were used. The tests showed that using AdaBoost makes the suggested methods work better. In addition, the improved processes led to better results than the old methods. The research's findings support the efficacy of creating fraud identification methods for e-commerce platforms utilizing automated ML techniques. Through adopting the results of the research into practice, banks may be able to lower the time and money required to create and update active platforms against fraudulent payments and increase the efficiency of money transaction surveillance.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Charity System Model based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Blockchain technology is emerging as a revolutionary solution for improving transparency, trust, and accountability in the charitable sector. This paper introduces a blockchain-based model for a charitable system aimed at resolving significant issues in conventional charitable frameworks, including insufficient transparency, elevated administrative expenses, and donor skepticism. The proposed model employs decentralized ledger technology and smart contracts to establish a secure, verifiable, and tamper-resistant donation process, enabling donors to monitor funds and guaranteeing that donations are allocated in accordance with specified conditions. This model enhances donor trust and mitigates operational inefficiencies by reducing intermediaries through the implementation of blockchain technology. The results demonstrate the model’s capacity to enhance the integrity of charitable operations and underscore the significance of regulatory and accessibility factors for broad implementation.

articleTitle: Enhanced Ransomware Classification with a Hybrid RF-SVM Framework Using PCA and RFE
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Ransomware has grown rapidly and constantly, making it a serious threat to cyber security systems, thus necessitating more effective and robust classification methods. The hybrid approach SVM and RF with two advanced feature selection practices, i.e., Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), to improve ransomware classification. This is to achieve a compromise between computational efficiency on one side and classification accuracy on the other. Experimental results from a benchmark ransomware dataset indicated that the RF model attains the premier accuracy of 99.16%, followed by the hybrid RF-SVM model at 98.70%. In contrast, the SVM model has an accuracy of 93.12%. From these findings, it can be concluded that the hybrid RF-SVM technique performs better than all other models for detecting ransomware in real-life scenarios.

articleTitle: IoT-Driven Cold Chain Management for Real-Time Monitoring and Alerts for Perishable Goods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: As more temperature-sensitive goods are required to be transported safely, the demand for cold chain facilities has overtaken normal growth in the common market place. Things such as fresh fruits and vaccine are products that when taken to markets as a tool and useful for the people, depends greatly on maintaining adequate temperature for the product during the entire supply chain. Conventional storage monitoring is not effective as it limits the use of boring routine manual temperature checkups or temperature data recap done away from the premises. Thus, it is not uncommon for many cold chains to encounter temperature fluctuations without being noticed until it is too late; thereby resulting in wastage, costs, and risks to safety. Lately, the development of cold chain management has been greatly assisted by the advent of internet of things technologies. IoT creates an opportunity to link up everyday working equipment and facilitate geographical approaches by way of collecting data without human interference. With the help of IoT incorporated into cold chain logistics, business owners are able to monitor temperature-sensitive products regardless of their location in the supply chain in real-time. This minimizes time wastage caused by a slow investigation process in the event of any discrepancies and helps manage the product’s quality during the entire supply chain. It also helps avoid the burden of manual collection and analysis of environmental information since it can be done via smart devices.There is a strong possibility of applications of IoT in cold chain management processes; however, it is observed that there is a limited use of available technology in this respect, where many of these solutions are oriented toward specific problems, such as temperature control only, and overlook an array of other equally important issues like humidity and CO2 concentration. This is important because a reasonable number of essential elements are not only measured but also well taken care of by a discipline so as to avoid possible inefficiencies. This elucidates this gap by proposing a system that leverages the power of the Internet of Things to enhance cloud-based data logging and instant notification systems to improve cold chain logistics. It goes without saying that, in today’s logistics chains, where products are not only moved but also stored, constant control over temperature conditions of perishable items throughout the supply chain becomes an ever-increasing challenge in the cases of food, medicine and biotechnology industries. Cold chain logistics serve the purpose of spoiling the save if the right environmental conditions are not maintained for the specific product, these conditions are usually referred to as storage and transportation critics. Although the logistics industry has improved over the past few years, real-time tracking of important parameters such as temperature, humidity and carbon dioxide is still a challenge even today. To solve this challenge, Smart technologies, particularly of the Internet of Things category, provide a way out where all monitored values are continuously recorded, the data recorded and actions taken, if any, returned within the required time. This paper addresses the cold chain processes of perishables management and monitoring using the internet of things, and guarantees better control of the environmental factors within the supply chain processes.

articleTitle: Detecting Phishing Emails Using Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Phishing attacks exploit gaps in email security, posing considerable threats to both individuals and organization. This paper examines the practice of Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques for detecting phishing emails, building on traditional methods and integrating advanced machine learning models. The tools and technique used to carry out the research work, specifically for classification and analysis of phishing content are Named Entity Recognition (NER), BERT and GPT-4 which permit the identification of linguistic patterns, sentiments and syntactic structures unique to phishing emails. The paper summarizes with a discussion of the implications of these findings and potential for further refining NLP tools to strengthen cybersecurity measures against phishing attacks.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Conditional Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks in Brain Tumor Image Classification: A Novel Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In this paper, we explore the impact of conditional Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (cDCGANs) with brain tumor image classification and introduce a new way to improve diagnosis accuracy. Shortage of Data/Data Imbalance: In Medical Imaging datasets, it helps in surging the data scarcity and class imbalance with mimicking generation images using cDCGAN. The detailed investigation demonstrates that synthetic data effectively improves classifier performance by acting as a form of augmentation, providing additional training examples for classifiers and serving as ground truth. From the computational efficiency analysis, we see that there is also scalability in training time with respect to dataset size. Consequently, this study presents cDCGANs as an important asset with which to improve diagnostic accuracy through brain tumor categorization in clinical contexts.

articleTitle: Next-Generation CRM: AI, IoT, and the Future of Customer Relationship Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Customer relationship management helps an organisation for handling the customers and management of customer data to achieve healthy relationship with the customers. Integration of data from various sources including sales marketing and customer service applications. CRM is capable of storing enormous customer data for best better understanding of their customers for better understanding of the customers. Smart devices equipped with artificial intelligence and Internet of things serves as next generation CRM. It can be used as wearable devices for real time access of services and products related information anytime anywhere for getting the data of customers related to health indicator, activities, fitness details, location and purchase interest. Artificial intelligence, Internet of Things and machine learning are the future of customer relationship management to replace human intelligence. The advancements in technologies increase the efficiency of CRM software. The system manages the contact details and other data of the customers automatically. CRM manages the purchases, submissions of forms and emails. The trained model takes the collected data, sales records for pattern identification.

articleTitle: Efficient Network Anomaly Detection and Mitigation Strategies for Large-scale Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Efficient Network Anomaly Detection and Mitigation Strategies for Large-scale Networks As the number of connected devices has increased so has the potential for malicious activities and network malfunctions. This study focuses on creating efficient mechanisms for real-time and accurate detection and avoidance of outliers in big Abstract-Efficient Strategies to Detect and Mitigate Network Anomalies in Large-scale Networks As more and more devices get connected to the internet, the chances of malicious activities and network failures only increase. To address this problem, this study develops efficient mechanisms for detecting and avoiding outliers in big data networks in real time and with high accuracy. The approaches proposed will utilize techniques as machine learning, data mining and network traffic analytics. The next step is to build out anomaly detection models that can identify and classify abnormal network behavior using these techniques. In addition, the methods will employ advanced data processing tools to detect vast quantities of network data in real-time to minimize false positive rates." Active learning theory: efficient and scalable, deployable to large-scale networks, anomaly detection and remediation methods. L7-QoS takes even the network one step ahead and thus increases the network quality by significantly decreasing the ratio of the hazardous operation or the error of the system. This work has important implications to any sector or organization where large-scale networks are important--including telecommunications, banking, and healthcare.

articleTitle: Network Threat Monitoring System Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In the current digital era, where cyberattacks are increasing rapidly, safeguarding networks from advanced threats is essential. Continuous monitoring and detection are vital to prevent data breaches, system disruptions, and financial losses. This paper introduces a Network Threat Monitoring System (NTMS) which continuously monitors network traffic going through PCs, servers, and office networks, detecting suspicious activities and possible cyber-attacks in real-time. It informs about intrusion detection in good time, so that administering authorities can take quick preventive measures for securing vital infrastructure and data. The system has ensemble learning to enhance its detection accuracy. It involves integrating several algorithms under machine learning categories like Gradient boosting and random forest in a way that identifies both known and new threats. Its stacking ensemble applies a meta-model processing the output of individual classifiers to enhance its capability to detect threats. This multi-layer architecture, thus, overcomes the limitations of standalone models for higher accuracy with fewer false positives. The proposed system has achieved better performance considering the real-time traffic and network security analysis from the NSL-KDD dataset. Such developments are envisaged to create adaptive and robust solutions against modern cybersecurity challenges.

articleTitle: Deepfake Detection: Leveraging InceptionResNetV2 and LSTM for Enhanced Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The antique adage "seeing is believing" is simply no longer actual, which has profound implications for a ramification of sides of our lives. Deepfakes are becoming less complicated and simpler to create as technology advances. In fact, with the right software program, you can do a part of it right out of your palm. it is challenging to pick out deepfakes. The capability of the human eye to differentiate among deepfakes has reduced. however, a few academics have tried to identify deepfake. Deepfakes are media that can be generated by synthetic intelligence (AI) using algorithms. Artificial intelligence algorithms are designed to understand the traits of both the supply and the target photo. Subsequently, the target image is positioned on the pinnacle of the supply photograph. Our goal is to pick out video deepfakes by way of utilizing deep getting-to-know neural networks which include InceptionResNetV2 and LSTM. With the usage of transfer learning and the pre-trained InceptionResNetV2 CNN for characteristic extraction and vector production, we were able to efficaciously assemble a deepfake detection version. The capabilities had been used to train the LSTM layer, and the confusion matrix that was produced offers us the accuracy of testing and validation. The corresponding version's accuracy for 20 and 40 epochs was 84.75% and 91.48%, respectively.

articleTitle: Sentence Embeddings Using n-Gram Features and Contrastive Learning for Multilingual Datasets
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This paper presents a method for sentence recognition using an enhanced n-gram combined with reverse learning, to address the challenge of multilingual sentence representation without parallel data deal with similarities. For two data structures in different languages, Word2Vec provides sentence embedding. Margin-based contrast loss matches sentence representations, highlights similarities across languages, and differentiates between languages. Strict negative sampling improves the embedding quality by selecting strong negative samples. The method is evaluated using internal sentence similarity tasks and two external classification measures. The results show stable learning in English data but highlight challenges in non-English data due to language-specific complexity. The findings reveal an imbalance between recall and F1 scores, highlighting the limitations of the current multilingual syntax when the data are not bilingual. This study highlights the importance of using advanced N-gram-based optimization and learning techniques to address multilingual semantic representation challenges and facilitate multilingual NLP applications.

articleTitle: Robust Brain Tumor Classification using Transfer Learning and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Brain tumor identification and categorization are inevitable during proper diagnosis and customized treatment. In this study, we propose a robust approach for automatic classification of brain tumors into four distinct categories: GMNP Tumor. In order to extract complex features from medical imaging data, a CNN architecture is introduced to take advantage of the transfer learning framework. The CNN architecture pre-trained with general image information is further trained with a select subset of brain images to provide the model specific knowledge for the classification of tumors. The proposed transfer learning strategy is expected to improve generalization performance of the model and do well even when labeled data is scarce. It involves a variety of brains scans of patients with different types of tumors and ‘normal’ brains. While training, the CNN discovers the patterns distinguishing various classes of tumors, which also helps in the effective classification of GMNP Tumor. The findings of this research provide valuable input towards the current initiatives in applying complex deep learning methodology in medical image analysis for improved brain tumor detection and classification.

articleTitle: Handcrafted AI: Designing Virtual Hardware for Hand Gesture-Based Interaction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Hand Gesture Recognition (HGR) is a groundbreaking technology in computer vision that translates hand movements and configurations into computer commands, enabling more natural and intuitive interactions. HGR operates through a three-stage process: hand localization, feature extraction, and gesture recognition. First, the system identifies the hand region within an image or video frame. [1] Then, it extracts key features, such as the shape, orientation, and fingertip positions of the hand. Finally, it interprets these features to recognize specific gestures. Gestures are broadly categorized into static and dynamic types. Static gestures involve fixed hand postures, which are easier to detect but less expressive, while dynamic gestures consist of sequences of movements that convey richer information but require more complex processing. The potential applications of HGR are vast, particularly in human-computer interaction (HCI), where it can facilitate device control, virtual environment navigation, and real-time sign language interpretation.[2] Additionally, it can be integrated into gaming, education, and augmented reality for more immersive and interactive experiences. Despite its promise, HGR faces challenges such as complex backgrounds, varying lighting conditions, and occlusions, where parts of the hand are obscured. [3] Designing robust algorithms that ensure accurate real-time gesture recognition remains a key area of research. As these algorithms become more sophisticated and hardware capabilities improve, HGR systems are poised to play a significant role in the future of human-technology interactions.

articleTitle: Utilization of Digital Twin in Sustainable Infrastructure Development
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Industrialization and its impact have left its remarkable mark in human history which has further formulated a brighter future for our kind. The role of infrastructure has been primal in this regard and has evolved drastically over the years. As we look forward to achieve a more productive and sustainable future the United Nations have proposed certain goals to attain that. The aim of this paper is to focus on two of those goals namely sustainable infrastructure development and making cities more resilient via the perspective and implementation of digital twin in the construction industry. The paper defines digital twin and provides an overview over its usage in the industry along with its collaboration with other technologies like IOT (Internet of Things) and AI with respect to previous studies done by other papers. Components of digital twin have been discussed with suitable diagrams and detailed tables. After a detailed discussion on creditable sources referenced in the paper, certain limitations and research gaps have been identified which can be further resolved with the aid of certain suggestions mentioned in the latter part of the paper. Finally, with a view to improving the future prospects of research, this paper provides guidance on how to examine role, implementation and use of Digital Twin technologies in the construction sector by means of an Industry Specific Lens while setting limits and suggestions for addressing them.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security in Medical Imaging: Optimized Nature-Inspired Algorithms for Robust Watermarking in Gray scale Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The significance of watermarking grayscale medical images lies chiefly in ensuring data security and integrity especially in telemedicine applications. Watermarking is enhanced by the use of nature based algorithms that relies on biological processes and natural phenomena as heuristics for optimizing both embedding and extraction functions. The watermarking capacity against different attacks like compression, noise or even geometric distortions can be greatly improved using these algorithms. A number of nature based algorithms employed in this paper include: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Firefly Algorithm (FA) that have significant potential for securing grayscale medical image watermarking systems. This approach makes use of the adaptive and evolutionary aspect of such algorithms thus achieving high level of imperceptibility together with robustness at the same time inputs are secured while maintaining quality disappointing images. Through a thorough comparison and analysis the paper shows how such algorithms can enhance watermarking techniques leading to a better defense against unauthorized access or alteration of sensitive medical data.

Author Keywords: Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Firefly Algorithm (FA)

articleTitle: Potential of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: As stated by the president of the UN heath agency artificial intelligence has vast potential to improve the health of many of people around the world if ethics and human rights are central to its design. deployment, and use. The UN also recognized the need through Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 3, 9 and 10) regarding Al adoption in health care. With this motivation, the research aims to discuss the significance of artificial intelligence and in Health care and its different components like Diagnosis and disease Prediction, treatment personalization, healthcare Operations Management the study also discusses different network that are implemented in AI like ANN, CNN, DNN, additionally we also address some algorithms that are being used like SVM, LSTM, decision tree. Finally, the article discusses the difficulties and recommendation for the effective implementation of Al in healthcare the Natural Language Processing (NLP) Expert system, Computer vision, are few of the major recommendation that are discussed in this study for future enhancement of Al in heath cane.

articleTitle: IT Carrer Skills Prediction Based on Students Interest, Abilities and Computer Language Proficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In today's technology-driven landscape, predicting the career skills of IT students is essential for aligning academic education with industry needs. This research explores the prediction of IT career skills based on students' interests, abilities, and proficiency in computer languages, along with specific project experiences and future career aspirations. The dataset, comprising hundreds of samples rows and number of features—such as Interested Domain (for example - Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cyber security), Projects (e.g., Chatbot Development, Data Analytics, E-commerce Website), and Computer Language Proficiency (e.g. Strong, Average, Weak) where machine learning-based model will predict Future Career Skills (e.g., Machine Learning Researcher, Data Scientist, Software Engineer) etc for students. Several models were evaluated, with the Random Forest Regressor demonstrating the highest predictive power, achieving an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.9631, corresponding to a prediction accuracy of 96.31%. The model's performance was further validated through its low Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 8.61 and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.80, indicating its effectiveness in forecasting students' potential career paths. This study provides actionable insights by mapping students' project experiences and domain interests to relevant IT career paths, enabling educators and career counsellors to offer tailored guidance. The findings also help students align their academic projects with future job roles, improving career readiness and employability in specialized fields such as Machine Learning, Cyber security, and Cloud Computing.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Advanced Animal Image Classification Using the Xception Model: Achieving High Accuracy in Diverse Species Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This work investigates the advanced deep-learning features of the Xception model for image classification of 15 animal species. The Xception model known for its depthwise separable convolutions showcased remarkable performance in animal picture categorization using a dataset from Kaggle consisting of 30,000 training images, 2,000 validation images, and 2,421 testing images. Particularly for classes like Beetle and Cat, the model obtained an amazing overall accuracy of 96% on the test set with strong precision and recall scores. The full classification report and confusion matrix highlight even more the model's ability to precisely distinguish between closely related species and expose areas that might use work. Effective learning and generalization were verified by analysis of training and validation losses; persistent low values indicate the stability of the model. High training and validation accuracy show how well the model can manage observed as well as unseen data. The findings confirm the strength and possible uses of the Xception model in interactive learning tools, animal research, and monitoring of biodiversity. This work emphasizes the efficiency and flexibility of the model in the field of computer vision, therefore advancing automated animal image classification.

articleTitle: Enhancing predictive accuracy and interpretability through Explainable Deep Ensembles learning for lung cancer classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In the era of Artificial Intelligence, applications in healthcare, banking, and autonomous vehicles have been significantly enhanced and simplified through machine learning and deep learning models, collectively known as Artificial Intelligence. The models are developed to produce efficient predictive outcomes. When a machine learning (ML) model underperforms, combining weaker and stronger models can lead to a more effective and efficient result. In deep learning, the "Black Box" nature of models presents a challenge regarding transparency, commonly referred to as "Explainability". To address these challenges, we proposed a novel approach that integrates the robustness of the average Ensemble technique with saliency maps to enhance Explainability in multiple Deep neural networks (X-DEL). This approach aims to improve accuracy while identifying the most significant features contributing to the decision-making process. The model is applied to a lung cancer dataset to classify types of pathological lung cancers. Our novel method, compared to traditional ML algorithms, achieved an accuracy of 98%. Furthermore, it identified that features 0, 20, 30, and 50 have higher saliency values, suggesting they are more influential in the decision-making framework.

articleTitle: AI POWERED Cryptography for Secure Machine-to-Machine (M2M) Communication in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The Internet of Things' (IoT) next generation of computing depends on mobile ad hoc networks, or MANETs. In a MANET, every device has the ability to move in any direction. By offering cloud services to MANET subscribers, data processing and resource management can be managed across each element, enabling users to access smart devices within the IoT framework. MANET is vulnerable to a variety of attacks that reduce network performance. Only active network layer assaults are the subject of this study. We have implemented the SAODV protocol to improve security and performance in MANETs, and our solution makes use of hybrid cryptography techniques (RSA and DES algorithms) on SAODV. This study compares the AODV and SAODV routing protocols of MANETs using simulations of several factors, including energy, packet delivery ratio, and throughput. The suggested method can improve communication network security and identify new positions by employing a Machine-To-Machine (SD-M2M) approach. The NS2 network simulation environment is used to execute the suggested cryptographic routing method. The proposed method achieves high throughput, high packet delivery ratio, and low energy usage compared to the traditional method.

articleTitle: Secure Network Topology Design and Management Using Artificial Intelligence Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Network topology Designing and management of secure networks is designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data in a networked environment. Due to the increase in advanced cyber-attacks, traditional network security approaches are no longer enough. In this regard, an AI framework can be used to protect the network structure. It was an AI framework that used algorithms and machine learning techniques to analyze data traffic and detect vulnerabilities in the network. The framework uses these analyses to adapt network configurations and optimize security protocols in real time, thus making it more resilient against threats. In addition, the AI framework not only allows but enables dynamic network management naturally. Its ability to identify and adapt to stray network behaviors, whether they are from malware or denial-of-service attacks, allows it to mitigate those threats and ensure consistent performance and security. Besides, the framework of AI can also help in designing network topology, keeping in view network traffic patterns, user behavior, and possible attack vectors. This creates a stronger and more efficient network topology that is better designed to withstand security threats. The AI Framework for Network Topology Design and Management is a sophisticated approach that combines advanced algorithms, machine learning techniques, and expert knowledge to optimize network performance and ensure cost-effective security.

articleTitle: Personalized User Interaction in Web Applications using Adaptive LLM Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The rapid evolution of web applications has made personalization and intuitive user experiences increasingly essential. The aim of this work is to provide a tailored large language model (LLM) architecture allowing context-aware interactions within online contexts. Using real-world datasets like as Microsoft COCO and Amazon Customer Reviews enhanced with contextual metadata and behavioural analytics, we taught LLMs to grasp customer wants via explicit patterns and contextual signals. To allow the models to dynamically modify their replies, improve user engagement, and expedite processes, sophisticated natural language processing methods and contextual embedding strategies were used. In comparison to conventional static models, extensive experimentation and user testing exposed notable increases in user happiness and interaction efficiency. Significant problems like data privacy, model scalability, and real-time processing were resolved to guarantee the feasibility of these bespoke LLMs throughout several web application environments.

articleTitle: Fake Currency Detection Using A.I
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Counterfeit currency is significantly damaging the global economy. It causes problems for financial systems and makes people lose trust. Right now, fake currency detection systems work well, but they often do not have easy-to-use features like being accessible and giving voice feedback in real-time. This paper presents a new app that can detect fake currency and includes a voice assistant. The voice assistant gives immediate feedback on whether the currency is real or not. This solution is designed to help people who have visual impairments and those who need to quickly check if currency is real in busy places. The system uses machine learning and computer vision to find fake currency, and it has a voice feedback feature to announce the results. "The system achieved an accuracy of 95% on a dataset of 10,000 images of real and fake currency notes."

articleTitle: AI for Disaster Management: Predictive Models and Response Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) in managing severe weather events has become more necessary in recent years owing to their increased frequency. Disaster management is required to control and avoid such occurrences. To successfully aid in better and quicker reactions to catastrophes, AI is widely employed in prediction and disaster preparation, damage mitigation and minimization, and rescue phases. To determine how AI technology can be used to lessen the damaging impacts of different disasters, this article looks into the potential for connecting artificial intelligence methods based on technological innovation. The study potentially contributes in designing an effective framework for disaster management based on the predictive accuracy and response time.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis Of Indonesian Twitter Users Towards Panna Cotta
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The food and beverage industry (F&B) is a business that has the main task of serving foods and beverages to consumers to provide customer satisfaction in terms of taste, quality, appearance, serving service, and atmosphere. Dessert is one of the things that is included in the fields of F&B and is related to current trends. One of the popular desserts is panna cotta which is a dessert from Italy that has a soft and jiggly texture and melts in the mouth. This paper investigates the use of social media, specifically Twitter, to study the social representations of people in Indonesia towards a classic Italian dessert named panna cotta. This paper aims to explore people's content and sentiment towards panna cotta. In particular, this study focuses on people's perception on panna cotta which can help businesses to determine whether people in Indonesia are interested in panna cotta, what makes them interested, and what flavours are preferred by them. In this research, the data was collected for analysis and divided into 3 categories: positive, neutral, and negative.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Movie Reviews Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This paper delves into the critical role that machine learning plays in the accurate classification of sentiments expressed in movie reviews. Throughout the study we research and apply NLP using deep learning and machine learning algorithms to train and test our IMDb 50K movie reviews dataset on different models and feature embedding to compare their accuracies and choose the most optimal model for sentimental analysis. Ultimately, using deep neural network model BERT neural gives us the best accuracy of 94.2% compared to lexicon-based approaches due to the limitations in feature extractions like Bag of Words and TF-IDF.

articleTitle: A Triage System Based Approach With AI-Driven Management In Bugs Resolving Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Software bugs management is one of the most crucial and time-intensive jobs for software development teams. With this ground reality, there is an urgent need to build a robust system to identify, prioritize, and fix bugs. In this paper, we present a new methodology for handling bugs, which incorporates a triage system and AI-powered methods to assist with bug management. Our triage system is a classification model to classify bugs of severity, impact, or urgency. This aids in prioritizing bugs and the workforce required to fix them. The system also uses AI to detect the issue, and special techniques like natural language processing and machine learning are used to automate the triage process. The proposed novel approach, which is AI-based, also incorporates a bug resolution management system that uses predictive analytics to deliver a forecast of how many developers need to work on a bug and how much time would be needed to resolve it based on historical data., which allows for quick and efficient detection and classification of bugs as manual effort is minimized from the dev teams. The statistical data regarding the number of bugs reported per module allows for better planning and allocation of resources, thus increasing the overall efficiency of the bug resolution process.

articleTitle: Wireless Network Coverage Optimization Through Dynamic Topology Control
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Wireless network coverage providing uniform coverage across a broad spatial domain can prove to be complicated. In this context, Dynamic Topology Control has been introduced as a potential approach to maximize the coverage area of wireless networks. DTC utilizes the current state of the network environment to dynamically adapt the transmission power and topological connections of nodes in the network. Using DTC allows the network to dynamically adjust the transmission power of the nodes to achieve proper signal-to-noise, thus optimizing the network coverage. Moreover, DTC also supports adding/removing a node to/from a mobile campaign (from a mobile campaign means a mobile campaign uses/up. This ensures resource optimization and reduces node interference, leading to better network coverage. The ground simulations and field trials have also proven the efficiency of DTC over traditional static approaches in enhancing the coverage of the network. In addition, the technology is adaptable to various forms of wireless networks and thus can be applied to many scenarios. Therefore, direct-time-cyclic transmitters are an effective means of increasing and improving coverage in wireless networks, which can be helpful in modern wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: Edge AI in 6G: Vision, Technologies, and Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The development of wireless connections is being pushed by an unprecedented rise of artificial intelligence (AI) software, with 6G becoming a game-changing technology. However advanced artificial intelligence (AI) needs a lot of connectivity and processing power, which causes delays, energy waste, network traffic, and privacy breaches. By combining sensing, interaction, computing, and intellect, Edge AI—which incorporates model learning and reasoning capacities at the connection's edge—offers an innovative approach for 6G network deployments. With an emphasis on distributed machine learning algorithms and incorporated wireless networking protocols, this article offers a vision for sustainable and reliable edge artificial intelligence (AI) systems. To fit edge AI, the article also covers novel design concepts, service-driven utilization techniques for optimizing, and a complete end-to-end system framework.

articleTitle: Enhancing Breast Cancer Diagnosis with Vision Transformers: A Novel Approach using MaskGuided Attention for Ultrasound Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Deep learning models, notably convolutional neural networks (CNNs), demonstrate great promise in medical image processing. Nonetheless, CNNs frequently encounter challenges in capture holistic context and long- range dependencies in high-resolution images, which are crucial for accurate medical diagnostics. A new state-of-the-art technique called Vision Transformers (ViTs) uses self-attention mechanisms for gathering global correlations between image patches, thereby addressing some of the inherent limitations of CNNs. This study investigates the application of ViTs for diagnosing breast cancer from ultrasound images of tumor. The findings suggest that ViTs not only achieve competitive accuracy in identifying breast cancer lesions but also offer superior interpretability through attention mechanism, which can aid clinicians in understanding model decisions. This paper highlights the potential of ViTs as a powerful tool in medical imaging, particularly for breast cancer diagnosis, and outlines future research directions for enhancing clinical applicability.

articleTitle: Automated Kidney Anomaly Detection Using Deep Learning and Explainable AI Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of kidney abnormalities such as cysts and tumors is essential for timely and effective treatment. This paper describes an in-depth study on recognizing and identifying kidney abnormalities using CT imaging. Convolutional neural sneŧworks are popular due to their excellent ability to extract complex features from large amounts of medical data and achieve better results than conventional methods. The proposed method combines CNN and previous learning models, including VGG16, EfficientNetB0, and MobileNetV2, all optimized to improve performance and robustness across multiple kidney types. The model shows good specificity in classifying some cases, helping to make more reliable diagnoses. Additionally, descriptive artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques such as LIME and SHAP are used to improve the model by identifying key features that affect the cut-off. This helps increase radiologists’ confidence, improve interpretation, and facilitate clinical decision-making. The results show that this model has the potential to help improve early diagnosis, ultimately improving patient outcomes and diagnostic procedures.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Soil Analysis for Crop Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Agriculture is a crucial part of India's economy, contributing over 17% to the nation's GDP (Gross Domestic Product), engaging over 60% of the workforce but still the effort-to-yield ratio of the sector remains significantly low. Analyzing soil properties, such as temperature, pH, humidity, water retention capacity, etc., helps determine soil quality, which is crucial for optimal agricultural productivity. This assessment later recommended crops that align with soil conditions and external environments, maximizing yield potential, and sustainable land management thereby preventing degradation. Similar to most studies aimed at advancing agriculture, the main objective of this research is to drive development by implementing ML-based models for crop classification. This paper presents a comparative analysis of various machine learning including KNN, SVC, Random Forest, etc on a single dataset. The comparative analysis highlights the advantages of each algorithm over others, helping to select the best-suited model to be implemented for real life applications. Our findings prove that the Random Forest algorithm outperforms the others, achieving the highest accuracy of 99.24%.

articleTitle: Neural Network Innovations in Next-Generation Optical Fiber and WDM Networks: Tackling Signal Degradation and Resource Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Neural networks have been included in optical fiber communication along with WDM networks, which have demonstrated new paths for increasing such systems' performance, availability, and effectiveness. Optical fiber communication used for high data rates suffers from signal attenuation, noises and nonlinearities, especially at longer transmission distances. Neural networks provide solutions through identifying/recognizing complicated signal patterns and at the same time correcting the existing distortions on a real-time basis. They can be used for such applications as signal equalization, nonlinearity correction, and noise removal, and can enhance data transfer quality by many times. When several data channels are carried out simultaneously using different wavelengths, it is found that neural networks are very effective in controlling the WDM networks. They are capable of predicting the traffic pattern, doing dynamic resource allocation efficiently, and providing an optimized routing and wavelength assignment (RWA) model compared to conventional techniques. In addition, with the development of neural networks, OPM functions are brought to a higher level in terms of speed and accuracy of the assessment of other important optical metrics, including OSNR and chromatic dispersion. Furthermore, such networks can also recognize possible faults, thus providing stable and reliable communication. A continued increase in the requirement of data transmission rate makes the use of neural networks in optical fiber communication and WDM systems crucial in handling the main issue, providing innovative and optimized solutions for future-generation communication systems

articleTitle: Analyzing Body Language and Facial Expressions Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Body Language decoding is an important aspect of understanding human emotions, intentions, and personality by interpreting non-verbal cu es. It helps to get insights into human behavior, mindset, and psychology of the person. AI Body Talk is a software system that is capable of detecting and interpreting the body language of a person in real-time inference. It can recognize the sign language along with face, hand, and pose estimation with immediate feedback. It empowers the minority group of society who use sign language to communicate in society equipped with the Mediapipe to train custom models with its pre-built solutions to detect face landmarks, hand-tracking, and pose estimation. The results exemplify the system’s potential for various applications like monitoring audience distraction, inspecting interviewee personality, understanding cultural sensitivity, diagnosing patients' health, and more.

articleTitle: The Ethical Implications of AI in Management: Navigating Challenges in Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This research uses a tutorial approach to explore the intricate link between artificial intelligence (AI) and management decision-making processes, focussing on the alignment problem, which is a crucial obstacle to ensuring AI systems are in line with moral principles and human values. When defining artificial intelligence, it looks at a variety of methods, including algorithmic methods for machine learning (ML), sentiment analysis, anomaly detection, recommendation systems, expert systems, neural networks, deep learning, data visualisation, and natural language processing. The investigation explores how methodologies for machine learning and predictive analytics may use massive datasets to assist organisations in identifying market dynamics, competitive landscapes and novel patterns. By boosting data-driven decision-making, machine learning (ML) helps businesses proactively adjust to shifting circumstances and take advantage of new opportunities. Additionally, by analysing likely outcomes and their associated probabilities, this study investigates how ML-driven prediction models may lower risks. The investigation also looks at the ethical conundrums that arise when managers utilise ML to make strategic decisions, highlighting the significance of fairness, responsibility, and transparency in decision-making using algorithms.

articleTitle: Smart Resume Analyzer: An Automated Approach for Recruitment Process
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This work presents an automated Resume Analyzer system to streamline the initial resume screening process. Designed to alleviate recruiters’ workloads, the system extracts key resume details—such as name, contact information, experience, and qualifications—without manual input. This system leverages Natural Language Processing (NLP) and text mining. A novel scoring mechanism evaluates resumes based on the presence of essential elements like declarations, interests, and skill sets. This web tool provides a resume score which is used by organization and applicants to review about it. This tool allows recruiters to assess resumes in PDF with a rating rapidly, saving them both time and effort. The SVM algorithm outperformed kNN, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree and Random Forest.

articleTitle: Game Theory-Based Power Control in Cooperative Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Power control based on game theory has been proposed as a tool by which the efficiency and performance of cooperative wireless networks can be achieved. The method applies theoretical concepts from game theory, which focuses on the interactive decisions made by a group of agents to direct power across various nodes on the network effectively. Game theory-based power control aims to achieve such a compromise between individual shocker performance and network-wide performance. Instead of independent agents pursuing their utility, nodes in our solution form a cooperative environment that works towards a common goal whilst maximizing their utility functions. If appropriately designed, cooperative power control can improve network coverage and spectrum efficiency and reduce interference and energy consumption. Dynamic Transmission Power Control in CDMA-based Systems Using Game Theory Optimal resource allocation and improved overall network performance can be achieved when nodes are able to dynamically adjust their transmit power in response to the characteristics of the observed channel conditions and network dynamics. In this paper, we contribute to the existing literature on the game theory-based cooperative wireless networks with emphasized fundamentals and advantages. This approach is shown to be effective in the sense of optimal power allocation through various simulation results and improving the overall network performance.

articleTitle: Exploring blockchain solutions: Integrating cryptocurrency with IoT for enhanced security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Blockchain, initially developed as the underlying technology for Bitcoin, has garnered significant attention for its applications beyond cryptocurrency, particularly in complex non-monetary domains. Utilizing cryptographic methods like hashing and asymmetric encryption, combined with a distributed consensus model, Blockchain-based ledgers achieve high levels of security and immutability, effectively removing the need for third-party intermediaries. Meanwhile, the rapid growth in Internet of Things (IoT) devices being connected to networks raises substantial concerns around security and privacy. Addressing these security challenges is essential for the expanding IoT landscape. This paper explores the blockchain solution by integrating cryptocurrency with IoT for enhanced security, reviewing recent studies and applications to evaluate Blockchain's role in IoT security, pinpoint challenges, and propose Blockchain-driven solutions to improve security in the IoT ecosystem.

articleTitle: Harnessing IoT and Machine Learning for Efficient Water Management in Urban Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This paper sees the opportunity to respond to the current and global issue of water management by proposing a smart water management system that uses IoT, cloud computing and the application of ML algorithms. On one hand, the conventional approaches to water management are not enough to satisfy the needs of urban systems; on the other hand, they cause excessive water loss and contamination. The flow rate, the pressure, and the water quality, pH and turbidity are examples of data of the proposed system that will be collected through IoT sensors placed in strategic locationsBy applying the state of the art Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Hybrid Gradient Boosting Machines (HGBM), the system is built to detect leaks, schedule the maintenance operations and detect contaminations. Besides, it employs features like EPANET to model water distribution systems under dynamic environments. It also makes the best use of available resources, safe guards the environment and nurtures sustainable urban growth. This work contributes to the subject by narrowing down the limitations regarding scalability, data integration, and privacy to offer a strong foundation for putting contemporary urban water utilities on a more sustainable footing for the benefit of the global community.

articleTitle: Harnessing NLP and AI for Reliable News Verification in the Digital Era
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The uncontrolled spread of fake information in this digital age poses a significant threat to public perception, political balance, and social unity. This paper presents a robust system for the discovery of fake news by means of advanced machine learning techniques and fuzzy logic. This system integrates natural language processing with machine learning models for the classification of news content as genuine or false, thereby attempting to limit the spread of misinformation. An overall labeled dataset is formed by data collection from multiple reputable news sources and fake news repositories. The text data is cleaned and tokenized and preprocessed with removal of stop words and stemming. Critical patterns are extracted from the articles by TF-IDF and word embeddings. Machine learning models, such as Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, and Neural Networks, are trained and evaluated using various metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Cross-validation ensures reliability. This research formulates a real-time user-friendly tool for news authenticity classification, limiting the spread of misinformation, and encouraging verified content sharing. This system, because of the introduction of fuzzy inference, is better suited to linguistics nuances. Thus, the system can prove to be very effective in terms of fake news.

articleTitle: Enhancement on Multi-speaker Speech Separation and Speaker Profiling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Multi-speaker speech separation is a process of separating audios of multiple speakers speaking at the same time in a real-life environment, recorded together. It is also called as overlapping speech separation. This research uses deep learning approach to separate the audios while maintaining the speaker information. Current state of the art tools/approaches have limited success in identifying and separating multiple speakers talking at the same time and are also susceptible to noise and reverberation. Our aim is to build upon and enhance approaches like Conv-TasNet, DualPath RNN, SepFormer and RE-SepFormer to separate speech of each speaker. Once the audios are separated, the system performs speaker profiling to get insights into individual speakers. Speaker profiling is a process of studying the MFCC and other features of the speech data and estimate more information about the speaker. Then the deep learning models are used to determine age, gender, accent, emotion, and such information of the speaker and generate speaker profiles. This system could be useful for transcribing any recorded meeting or gathering or event, where multiple speakers are speaking at the same time such as corporate meeting, notetaking, courtroom transcribing and group discussion. It is also could be used in surveillance system in crowded environment for detecting target speakers as well as target keywords spoken. Speaker identity-based intent detection in multi-user environment of manufacturing industry or any other such operations is also one of its major applications.

articleTitle: Personalized Dementia Prediction Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Early-stage dementia detection is a significant challenge in the healthcare field. Many individuals remain unaware of their cognitive decline until the condition progresses. This research aims to develop a personalized approach for predicting dementia. Multiple machine learning algorithms were applied to the dataset. Impressively, Random Forest model achieved a perfect accuracy of 98.75%.

articleTitle: Classification of Operational Records in Aviation Using Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Ensuring safety in the aviation industry is critical, even minor anomalies can lead to severe consequences. This study evaluates the performance of four different models for DP (deep learning), including Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BLSTM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Simple Recurrent Neural Networks (sRNN), on a multi-class classification task involving Commercial, Military, and Private categories using the Socrata aviation dataset of 4,864 records. The models were assessed using a classification report, confusion matrix analysis, accuracy metrics, validation loss and accuracy curves. Among the models, BLSTM achieved the highest overall accuracy of 72%, demonstrating superior performance in stability and balanced classification, while LSTM followed closely with 71%, excelling in recall for the Commercial class. CNN and sRNN exhibited lower accuracies of 67% and 69%, with significant misclassifications in the Private class. While the results highlight the strengths of BLSTM and LSTM in handling sequential dependencies and complex classification tasks, all models faced challenges with class imbalance, particularly in predicting the Military and Private categories. Addressing these limitations through data augmentation, advanced feature engineering, and ensemble learning techniques could enhance classification accuracy and robustness. This study underscores the importance of selecting appropriate architectures for domain-specific tasks and contributes to advancing deep learning applications in multi-class classification problems

articleTitle: Advancing Pediatric Appendicitis Diagnosis: Harnessing CNN and Hybrid Models with Ultrasound Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Pediatric appendicitis, an acute inflammatory disease, arises from the obstruction of the appendix, often due to inflammation or a fecalith. This common abdominal emergency in children presents diagnostic challenges due to its varied clinical manifestations, which can lead to misdiagnosis or higher perforation rates stemming from atypical symptoms. This research investigates the use of deep learning, more especially Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), by utilizing ultrasonic imaging data, which is less expensive, non-invasive, and quicker than the other approaches now in use. Several variants are evaluated including a basic CNN and more advanced hybrid models such as CNN-Support Vector Regression, CNN-Transformer, and Hierarchical Deep CNN, to identify the most optimal model to significantly enhance diagnostic accuracy, for young patients facing this condition. The study's main goal is to develop a highly accurate and dependable diagnostic tool for evaluating the severity of pediatric appendicitis by differentiating between simple and complex cases and identifying whether surgery is required to inform treatment plans. Various challenges that need to be tackled are managing significant dataset imbalances, enhancing interpretability and transparency for real-world clinical settings, and ensuring the robustness and adaptability of all these models across various healthcare environments.

articleTitle: Smart Ear Disorder Management with AI-driven Insights and Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Otoscopy is an essential diagnostic method for evaluating ear health and detecting diseases such as infections, inflammations, and structural anomalies. The precise classification of otoscopy images is, nonetheless, difficult due to the variety of diseases. This research presents a deep learning methodology utilizing the DenseNet structure for automated categorization of otoscopy images. A curated dataset, including normal anatomy and various diseases, was preprocessed for homogeneity and enriched for diversity. The model was trained utilizing categorical cross-entropy loss, accompanied by hyperparameter optimization to improve performance. The evaluation metrics, comprising accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC, confirmed the model's efficacy. The findings indicate that the suggested method attains a classification accuracy of 99.26%, highlighting its potential to facilitate the rapid and dependable diagnosis of ear diseases in clinical settings. The implementation of sophisticated data augmentation methods mitigates issues associated with restricted datasets, hence ensuring good model generalization. The suggested paradigm shows potential for incorporation into real-time diagnostic tools, addressing deficiencies in accessibility and skill in otological care.

articleTitle: Sign Ease: AI-Based Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The research aims to find how effective various models are based on deep learning, particulary—Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), VGG-16, MobileNet V2, Inception V3, and ResNet-50—on the ISL dataset, using transfer learning techniques with pre-trained ImageNet weights to improve model performance. We assess the models using rigorous evaluation metrics, including F1-score, accuracy, detection rate, loss, and specificity. Our results reveal that ResNet-50 outperforms the other models, achieving exceptional evaluation accuracy, specificity (98.41%), detection rate (99.27%), and F1-score (99.34%). The superior performance of ResNet-50 is attributed to its deep architecture, residual connections, and efficient handling of the vanishing gradient problem, which allow it to capture complex features more effectively. While VGG-16 shows promising results with a test accuracy of 97.37%, Inception V3 and MobileNet V2 demonstrate limited effectiveness, indicating their lower suitability for this specific task. These findings highlight the importance of model architecture in achieving high performance for the ISL dataset.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based security solutions for IOT networks: Analysing efficacy and implementation challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Blockchain innovation has gathered significant attention from both scholars and industry professionals after years of development. This technology enables the creation of smart contracts, which facilitate automated deal execution among users. Today, blockchain is also employed as a specialized infrastructure in some IT applications, helping prevent data duplication, similar to how Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies manage transaction records. Bitcoin records, for instance, are exceptionally secure as the currency circulates across hundreds of thousands of servers, making it nearly impossible to alter. For a successful breach, an attacker would need to manipulate records on 51% of these servers simultaneously. In contrast, private data stored on single servers, such as those managed by Amazon and Google, are more vulnerable to cyberattacks. In this paper, the study propose leveraging blockchain to address security concerns in the Internet of Things. The study identifies and categorizes common security challenges, with a focus on data privacy issues, as well as the protocols used for network organization, communication, and management. Following this, the study outline security solutions for IoT and illustrate scenarios in which blockchain is applied within IoT applications.

articleTitle: Barriers Among Novice Day Traders in the Gulf and AI-Driven Pathways to Success
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This study explores the barriers faced by novice day traders in the Gulf region using a qualitative phenomenological approach. It identifies seven major themes that influence decisionmaking and profitability, including emotionally driven decisions, selective scepticism, hyper-vigilant monitoring, inadequate financial knowledge, unreliable trading platforms, insufficient personalization, and information overload. These findings highlight the interplay of psychological, educational, and technical factors that hinder consistent trading success. By focusing on traders’ lived experiences, this study provides a deeper understanding of the challenges they encounter. It suggests that enhancing user-centred design, educational resources, and psychological support features within trading platforms could improve outcomes for novice traders. The study’s insights are intended to inform the development of tailored AI-driven tools, supporting more effective trading strategies for novices in this context.

articleTitle: From Traditional Banking to Fintech: Analyzing the Evolution of Online Loan Research
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This research provides a comprehensive analysis of the development of online loan studies. By analyzing 432 Scopus papers using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and bibliometric analysis, the study identifies key research topics, including traditional banking risks, peer-to-peer lending, and fintech innovations. The results highlight the growing interest in online loans, particularly in regions like China and the United States. The findings have significant implications for academia, policy-making, and the financial industry, though further research is needed to explore underrepresented regions and the practical impacts of Fintech on traditional banking systems.

articleTitle: The Impact of AI on High-Frequency Trading: A New Paradigm in Share Market Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: A fresh approach in financial trading has emerged as a result of the significant shifts in the dynamics of global share markets brought about by the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) into high-frequency trading (HFT). In order to analyse large datasets in real-time, perform trades in microseconds, and AI-driven Deep learning, machine learning, and natural language processing are all examples of things that HFT uses to help people make the best choices they can in markets that have to change all the time. This change will help people make better decisions, and sellers will be able to respond quickly to changes in the market. Individuals can trade faster, better, and for greater amounts of cash with it than ever before. AI does have some problems when used in HFT, though. It can make the market less stable, lead to legal problems, and make it more diligently to be fair and honest. The amount of money, how well markets work, along with the way risks are handled are all changed by AI. It also discusses about how AI changes HFT. This study talks about the pros and cons of HFT powered by AI. Along with the way shares are sold, it also hints at how it might change future rules.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Enhancing Security in Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Web of Things or IoT frameworks rely upon wireless communication systems or WCS to accumulate and send measurements, their norm of execution is in danger from security assaults. In IoT frameworks, the Steering Conventions that can be routing protocols for Lower-Power (RPL) and Misfortune Systems administration are fundamental for successful measurements move; in any case, attacks can seriously disable usefulness. Utilizing the change of steering insights, traffic fascination through maverick focuses, and information passages to destructive places, these weaknesses compromise the legitimacy of organizations. To work on RPL's security and execution quality, this examination proposes a progressive AI and ML framework. This strategy joins a support learning calculation for adaptable and versatile highways, an irregular timberland framework for exact traffic classification, and modified RPL goals that consider order results while pursuing directing decisions. Displaying shows that this approach keeps up with negligible jitter while accomplishing extensive enhancements in bundle dispersion extents, network speed, and deferral. Also, it further develops execution quality in IoT-based WCS and solidly gets the RPL convention by accomplishing an extraordinary acknowledgment rate, scarcely any misleading up-sides, and speedy responses to somewhere safe occasions. The study's conclusions provide significant additions to the area and give a thorough way to safeguard RPL against common safety risks
