articleTitle: Automatic Vehicle Number Plate Recognition: A Narrative review of End-to-end Workflow
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In the current era, technology helps a lot to enhance human experiences leading to smart city development, which includes optimized energy usage, better healthcare availability, minimal governance, and intelligent mobility. However, considering the increase in day-to-day traffic, intelligent mobility is crucial, and its effective implementation is ensures flawless vehicle movements. The primary goal of is to design and develop the Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). The effective ITS ensures automatic vehicle movement management, and automatic traffic rule violation detection, which heavily relies on Automatic Vehicle Number Plate Recognition (AVNPR). In this paper, we described end-to-end workflow of AVNPR including the technologies used in each stage, the benefits and drawbacks of each technology followed by the limitations. The proposed paper exclusively reviews the modern, state-of-the-art models and architectures, and pioneered works carried out within the research area of AVNPR and the recent advancements.

articleTitle: Allocation in Wireless Networks using Convex Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Dynamic allocation of spectrum resources in wireless networks, where access points and users require spectrum resources to communicate with each other. The existing approaches towards sharing resources cannot handle the dynamic changes of the network and, as a result, fail to manage network resources and degrade user experience efficiently. Therefore, a dynamic network model using convex optimization techniques has shown a potential remedy for efficient resource allocation in wireless networks. Dynamic network modelling is a method that develops a mathematical representation of the wireless network by considering the changeable characteristics of the wireless network. The model takes advantage of instantaneous network conditions, such as traffic load, channel status, user location, etc., to accurately predict the resources needed at any given time. Using the model obtained by the previous step with convex optimization algorithms, we optimize the network resource allocation to minimize interference and maximize the network capacity. Using this approach, network operators can efficiently respond to dynamic changes in the network, enabling optimal resource allocation and enhanced user experience. Furthermore, through convex optimization, we can guarantee optimality over resource allocation, confirming a reliable solution for the network. One tool in dynamic network modelling for resource allocation in wireless networks is convex optimization, which leads to optimal resource utilization, improved performance, and better user satisfaction.

articleTitle: Development and Simulation of a Robotic Arm Using ROS2: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This research focuses on the development and implementation of a physical robotic arm controlled using ROS2 and powered by an Arduino microcontroller. The project integrates advanced robotic software tools such as URDF for modeling, RViz2 for visualization, and MoveIt2 for motion planning, enabling efficient control of the robotic arm. A serial communication interface is established between a laptop and the Arduino to calculate and transmit joint angles for real-time actuation. The study explores the challenges of transitioning from simulation to physical implementation, including hardware limitations and communication latency. The results demonstrate the successful application of ROS2 for controlling a physical robotic system, with potential implications for robotics education, research, and industrial automation. This work serves as a foundation for future developments, such as incorporating sensor feedback and autonomous capabilities.

articleTitle: Detecting Digital Deception: A CNN-RNN hybrid Approach of Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Deepfake technology has forced digital deception to create high demand for detection tools. This paper presents an approach for deepfake video detection using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) architecture that targets the artifacts present in the output from the generative models including Generative adversarial network (GAN). This approach looks at many strategies in terms of frames, among them for frame comparison, feature extraction based on CNNs, and for the purpose of temporal analysis CNN with long-short-term memory (LSTM) networks. The described model is trained on the set of the genuine vs. forged images and videos and demonstrates quite stable results with respect to digital forging detection. It is discovered that this proposed model achieves higher accuracy than previously used detection approaches in addressing face-swapping and face-reenactment deepfakes. The findings of this research demonstrate that CNN & RNN based deepfake detection is promising for media forensics, as it advances multimedia security and digital media credibility. This proposed method shows an accuracy of 81% in the Deepfake Detection Dataset (DFDS), respectively, with a very reduced number of sample size of ⩽ 100 samples(frames). This promises early detection of fake contents compared to existing modalities.

articleTitle: AI and IoT in Digital Marketing: Enhancing Automation, Personalization, and Consumer Interaction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: An interconnected system of Internet-enabled devices that can collect and transmit statistics via a wireless connection without the assistance of people is known as the Internet of Things (IoTs). Accordingly, the IoT's seductive power is causing significant shifts in the current corporate environment. The digital marketing industry stands to gain the most from this innovation, which is currently causing major shifts in many other sectors. Using a variety of digital marketing strategies, this innovation gathers numerous types of consumer statistics. IoT technological advancements' impact on digital marketing tactics and customer interaction has emerged as a crucial research topic as it begins to pervade many facets of everyday existence. This investigation examines the application of IoT-based machine learning (ML) in digital marketing for the food business. To give ML-based suggestions, consumer data is analyzed, interests are identified, and conduct is predicted using ML approaches. The ensemble technique aggregates the results of multiple ML techniques to produce an individual forecast. The accuracy matrices graphs for the K-nearest neighbor and decision trees produced excellent estimations, with 100% accuracy and 0.0 error, correspondingly. The naïve Bayes method achieved 97.2% accuracy with a 0.029 error, successfully identifying the right tags across every category. The guided ensemble of 3 ML methods is demonstrated by effectively enhancing digital marketing tactics in the food distribution industry by reducing duration and expenses.

articleTitle: Intelligent Network Selection in Heterogeneous Wireless Environments Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In recent years, the demand for wireless communication has increased, leading to the emergence of dense and various heterogeneous wireless networks. Tip #1: Choose the Best Wireless Network. Most users might have multiple wireless networks available to them due to the connected nature of today's world. The fast development of wireless technologies leads to manifold networks, which renders network selection a painstaking process. In heterogeneous environments, where multiple networks coexist with different characteristics, these issues are compounded. Machine learning techniques are employed intelligently to predict the most suitable network choice for a user. It gathers and examines multiple indexes such as network parameters, user preferences, and environmental elements in order to predict the optimum network for the user. This helps the user get rid of searching and connecting to networks manually, thus allowing for a seamless and practical network selection experience. This approach will address Latency, Network connection speed, Network disconnection, and User experience. Moreover, figures out how the network selection process improves accuracy over time by adapting itself from past user interactions.

articleTitle: Chatbots and Customer Service: Enhancing Marketing Management with AI Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: By increasing engagement, expediting client contacts, and boosting satisfaction through AI-driven solutions, chatbot integration in customer service has revolutionised marketing management. With an emphasis on how model assessment techniques—such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score—can be applied to enhance chatbot efficacy in customer service scenarios, this paper investigates the role of machine learning models in optimising chatbot performance. In order to appropriately meet a variety of consumer demands, this research offers perspectives into the selection, training, and evaluation of chatbot models by analysing a range of AI technologies, such as natural language processing (NLP) and predictive analytics. The influence of chatbots on customer loyalty and retention is highlighted in this article, which also explores the benefits and limitations of utilising AI in real-time consumer interactions. According to research, well-considered ML models can produce more precise and sympathetic answers, which enhances brand perception and opens up new channels for CRM in marketing plans.

articleTitle: Explainable AI in Blockchain System for Decentralized Governance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Decentralized governance is going through radical changes due to the innovative use of blockchain which allows decisions to be made in a transparent, secure and more im- portantly, immutable way, without the authority of a single individual or party. Thus, the introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) in blockchain governing systems complicates such thing as transparency and trust, especially in the case of deep AI systems. But more on this later – this is where Explainable AI or XAI comes into the picture. XAI methods enable understanding of the reasons behind the choices made by AI models and solves the "black box" problem that is predominant in machine learn- ing. When applied to decentralised governance, XAI provides clarifications of AI’s decision making in such areas as voting, resource distribution and the enactment of smart contracts. This way, the stakeholders are confident that the decision-making is fair and impartial and this is made possible by the use of XAI. This paper aims to find out more about the applicability of XAI concept in blockchain –based governance systems in terms of bias and fairness in automated decisions and explanation of the decisions made. The reasons why interpretability plays the crucial role in decentralized systems are explained with the help of the comparison between the classical artificial intelligence and the Xin Intelligent. The study also looks at various use cases such as, Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs), and voting systems implemented on blockchain platforms and how XAI can enhance the performance of the governance systems. As this study shows, XAI is vital in building trust, improving responsibility, and guaranteeing balanced majorities in decentralized blockchain governance structures.

articleTitle: Image Captioning Using Deep Learning: Bridging the Gap between Vision and Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The process of writing educational captions for photos has evolved dramatically in recent years thanks to developments in deep learning technologies. The issue of fully understanding image content and creating logical, contextually relevant captions remains a serious difficulty despite notable progress. Image captioning is a crucial task that can be applied to editing tools, virtual assistants, image indexing, and assistance for people with disabilities. AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP) meet up in picture or image subtitling/caption, which is the test of making clear normal language phrases for pictures. Since profound learning strategies, Using Regional Neural Networks (RNNs) and Convolutions Neural Networking (CNN) for image extraction, which are as often as possible upgraded by consideration instruments, have been taken on, this interdisciplinary test has seen critical progressions. Text summarization, template construction, and information retrieval are the three main activities included in the suggested model. The both directions long short-term storage method is used to locate the written content utilizing every word in a phrase, extract the knowledge, and finally incorporate it within the semantically vector. This paper highlights the importance of deep learning as a whole while also examining the development of image inscribing, its important methodology, and state-of-the-art techniques. It additionally discusses the hardships, uses, and expected ways in this field.

articleTitle: Sign Language Recognition using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Sign language recognition is extremely pivotal for filling the void existing between those deaf or hard of hearing, and the rest of mankind. Computer vision advancement through deep learning techniques has been followed successfully with remarkable success across images. This research paper presents a comprehensive study on the application of CNN for sign language recognition. The primary objective is to develop an accurate and efficient system to recognize sign language gestures and translate them into corresponding text or speech. The proposed approach comprises a deep learning model trained as 3000 images collected from various datasets and online resources. The proposed deep learning model is trained in such way that it achieves the seem less efficiency on real time images that contains sign language on different scales and poses. The various outperformed metrics such as precision, recall and f1-score are also recorded. The model achieves 0.995%, 0.994%, and 0.992% accuracy during the testing session.

articleTitle: Safe and Reliable Live-Streaming Traffic Monitoring System using OpenCV and Yolov8
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Traffic monitoring is critical for avoiding fatal accidents on the roads as well as essential for ensuring that traffic rules are followed. An effective traffic monitoring system is made possible by cutting-edge computer vision technology, raising the standard of urban traffic safety and lowering the possibility of traffic accidents. The field of urban safety management will benefit greatly from this creative idea. This paper aims to create an automated traffic vehicle monitoring system using an object detection algorithm known as You Only Look Once Version 8 (YOLOv8). The model’s reliability has been enhanced by the use of the YOLOv8 framework for successful vehicle object detection, speed estimation within streaming videos, as well as for license plate recognition. YOLOv8 model is used to identify vehicle objects in every single frame. The model accurately detects vehicles, while the license plate recognition module extracts the text from diverse plate formats. The study’s conclusions are important because they could lead to the development of a real- time, highly accurate, and reasonably priced traffic monitoring system. Road safety might get significantly improved by this research.

articleTitle: Predicting LinkedIn Post Reactions: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Social media platforms have become a critical space for businesses to interact with their audience. LinkedIn, a professional networking platform, offers metrics like reactions, comments, and shares to gauge post engagement. This paper investigates a data-driven approach for predicting the number of responses to a LinkedIn post. Various features such as post content, company statistics (e.g., followers and connections), and media type are analyzed using machine learning models. The study compares the performance of multiple regression models and explores the importance of features, yielding valuable insights for optimizing LinkedIn post engagement.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies for a Sustainable World – A Survey of Indian Corporates
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The study aims to examine the significance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in contributing to the sustainable world. It aims to examine the affirmative and progressive impact of leveraging AI in achieving sustainability. In this study, ‘Environmental, Social and Governance’ (ESG) score was chosen as the chief metric for measuring sustainability. Bombay Stock Exchange Sensex Index (representing 30 blue chip and large cap companies) was taken as sample. The data pertaining to AI tools being deployed by Sensex companies were collected from the published annual and sustainability reports, press releases, corporate news, interviews of Chief Technology Officers in business dailies of the sample 30 companies of Sensex. For brevity, the sample 30 companies were classified into (a) Manufacturing (b) IT and Software and (c) BFSI sectors. ESG scores as per S&P (Standard and Poor) Global Index Services were collected. The study examined the top performers in manufacturing, IT and Software and BFSI sectors in terms of AI tools adoption for achieving sustainability across the three pillars of ESG namely, Environmental, Social and Governance. The study explored the role of AI tools for achieving sustainability by (i) Evaluating corporate sustainability (ESG) scores, (ii) Portfolio of AI and Digital tools leveraged (iii) Benchmarking ESG scores of select companies with industry maximum and industry average and a brief gap analysis was done to improve the overall ESG performance. The study attempted to explore the AI digital technology innovations and initiatives of Indian Start-ups.

articleTitle: Advances in Crop Monitoring Technologies: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Agricultural optimization and food security rely on effective plant monitoring. This essay probes the evolution and comparative analysis of modern technologies that are revolutionizing agricultural monitoring. In this paper, we show how artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning algorithms, and drones combined with the power of IoT sensors (smart agriculture) along rural data collection using remote sensing technologies will help to improve precision farm management by understanding the pros and cons in implementing these AI-driven new tools into smart devices capable of supporting higher crop yields and higher efficiency. Through a review of case studies and market trends, this article delves into how these technologies provide farmers with real-time data, predictive analytics, and actionable insights. Moral, monetary, and ecological reverberations of bonding these advances universally are likewise discussed. Ultimately, this comparative study to develop resilient and sustainable food production systems through the inclusion of modern technologies is an important opportunity for many difficult socioeconomic and climatic issues.

articleTitle: Optimizing Supply Chain Operations through Machine Learning: Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In order to create enduring partnerships that are essential to attaining long-term economic success, supply chain management, or SCM, is essential. Strict standards and decision-making procedures are necessary for efficient SCM, and they have a big influence on the final results. In order to efficiently manage inventory levels and logistical procedures, this study offers a complex ML system that combines demand forecasts and optimisation methods. For predicting demand, the approach uses a Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) model, taking advantage of its capacity to process time-series data and identify intricate trends. The algorithm achieves an impressive 96.4% forecasting of demand accuracy by examining extensive historical sales data and a variety of supply chain variables. In order to optimise inventory rules, the investigation also uses optimisation techniques, particularly Genetic Algorithms (GA) in conjunction with Simulated Annealing (SA). The model demonstrated significant improvements when implemented to an actual commercial logistics system. Notably, it reduced storage expenses by 19% and increased order fulfillment rates by 24%, proving its capacity for combining service standards with financial efficiency. The findings highlight the significant impact of ML on improving supply chain efficiency and show how it can result in significant cost savings and improve service quality.

articleTitle: A Real Time approach for detecting and counting Vehicles using OpenCV and NumPy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Vehicle detection and counting using OpenCV is a crucial aspect of modern traffic management systems. This mini project aims to develop a robust solution for detecting vehicles in real-time video streams and accurately counting them as they pass through a designated area. OpenCV, a popular computer vision library, is utilized for its extensive functionality and ease of implementation. First, the video stream is captured and processed to extract individual frames. Subsequently, each frame undergoes preprocessing techniques such as resizing, grayscale conversion, and noise reduction to enhance vehicle detection accuracy. Vehicle detection is achieved through the implementation of a deep learning- based object detection algorithm, such as YOLO (You Only Look Once) or SSD (Single Shot MultiBox Detector). These algorithms are trained on large datasets to recognize vehicles with high precision. Once vehicles are detected, a tracking algorithm is employed to maintain continuity between frames and accurately count the number of vehicles passing through the specified region of interest. This tracking algorithm ensures that vehicles are not double-counted and provides a reliable count for traffic analysis purposes.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Deep Learning for Weather Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Deep learning is a robust framework for solving complex prediction and forecasting problems from multiple fields, such as weather sciences. Due to the abundance and higher resolution of data available, cloud-based deep learning offers a compelling approach for achieving promising gains in accuracy and efficiency regarding weather forecasting. A more pressing priority in the face of worsening weather events requires faster and more reliable forecasting. Deep learning in the cloud is implemented by training deep neural networks on large datasets stored in a public or private cloud and subsequently using these pre-trained models to predict new data. This encourages using large-scale computational resources, such as those necessary to tackle the heavy data needed for precise meteorological forecasts. Such deep learning models have the flexibility and scalability required to adapt and tune them for specific weather patterns, which can then run on a cloud, enabling readiness as demanded. In this work, 3, x, y present a scalable deep learning-based approach to extended-range temperature prediction on high-performance cloud resources. We use the model to train on historical weather data combined with real-time observed weather from various sources.

articleTitle: Smart Antennas and Machine Learning: Enhancing Beamforming in Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: One of the most effective and widely used technological advancements for increasing capacity, enhancing quality, and expanding coverage in wireless communications systems is the smart antenna. Smart antennas are essential for increasing the effectiveness and dependability of wireless communication systems because they make use of cutting-edge signal processing techniques. Smart antennas' beamforming capability, which concentrates signal transmission and reception in particular directions, increases signal strength, lowers interference, and expands network capacity. As wireless networks become more complicated, machine learning (ML) has become a potent tool for beamforming optimisation. ML algorithms can proactively adjust antenna characteristics by using real-time data, learning from fluctuations in the environment to optimise performance. In order to improve beamforming capabilities, this research investigates the incorporation of ML with smart antenna systems. We go over several ML techniques, such as supervised and reinforcement learning, for resource allocation, user localisation, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) optimisation. Additionally, we draw attention to how deep learning might enhance spatial filtering, facilitating more effective communication in 5G and beyond. The potential direction for next-generation wireless communication networks is presented by the convergence of ML and smart antennas.

articleTitle: Combining Image Processing and Machine Learning for Object Detection in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The goal of object detection research is to address safety issues at industrial locations; yet, optimizing object detection efficiency while maintaining real-time capabilities is still difficult in complicated industrial settings. An unconditionally protected detector is proposed in this research to solve this issue. A bottleneck-structured residual block is used by the detector's backbone network to improve real-time performance and minimize computation. Additionally, a selective attentiveness network enhances object detection by recognizing important characteristics based on the neck structure's feature map's morphological attributes. The updated YOLOv4 model, Faster RCNN, and SSD on the COCO and KITTI datasets for object identification, is proposed in this research to address the aforementioned issues. Particularly important tasks requiring strong mathematical underpinnings are picture segmentation, object detection, and classification. Although there have been improvements, there are still issues, like the need to define terms like deep learning, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. A strong research foundation requires precise definitions and interpretations. The development of machine vision is a reflection of a bold attempt to mimic human eyesight. The ability to simulate human behaviour and perception has advanced remarkably thanks to interdisciplinary cooperation and using machine learning techniques.

articleTitle: Digital Agriculture Platforms: Empowering Farmers and Enhancing Market Accessibility
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In the present day and age of technology and digitalization our proposed platform revolutionizes the agricultural market concept by providing a direct connection between the farmers and the consumers thus reducing the middlemen and providing a clear and viable market solution. The system also benefits farmers in that it makes it easier for them to display their produce, set price and sell. By having extensive product catalogue, using multiple languages, and interacting through the website in real-time, farmers are able to directly deal with the buyers from their respective regions and they are fairly paid for their work. In turn, consumers get to enjoy new, fresh, local and affordable foods from the markets they get supplied to. The secure mode of payment and simplified interface makes it easily accessible for all clients to create a sustainable and positive impact on the economy of the agricultural sector.

articleTitle: Navigating Deepfakes with Data Science: A Multi-Modal Analysis and Blockchain-Based Detection Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Deepfake technology, fueled by advancements in artificial intelligence, presents a dual-use phenomenon with innovative applications in entertainment, education, and communication alongside significant ethical and societal risks, such as misinformation, identity theft, and privacy violations. This paper proposes a novel framework combining multi-modal analysis and blockchain verification to enhance deepfake detection. The multi-modal approach employs audio-visual analysis, temporal and spatial inconsistencies, and advanced feature extraction techniques to identify manipulations, while blockchain provides a tamper-proof mechanism for authenticating digital content at its source. By addressing research gaps such as cross-domain adaptability and limited training datasets, the framework offers a holistic solution to escalating challenges. Moreover, the paper emphasizes the importance of transparency, privacy preservation, and global collaboration to align technological innovation with ethical accountability. This work contributes to building a trustworthy digital ecosystem, enabling responsible applications of deepfake technology while mitigating its risks.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing Management: Enhancing Customer Engagement and Personalization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Marketing can use artificial intelligence (AI) to your advantage. It makes it easier to create intricate and sophisticated algorithms, expand the number of data and info sources, and improve software's capacity for data management. Brand-user interactions are changing as a result of AI. Machine learning (ML) is a type of artificial intelligence that allows computers to process and comprehend data without the need for explicit programming. In order to shed light on their functions in providing individualised experiences, this article explores crucial machine learning methods including clustering, content-based filtering, collaborative filtering, and predictive modelling. Examining real-world applications across a range of industries, such as retail, social media, email marketing, and e-commerce, highlights successful implementations. The essay examines the disadvantages, including concerns over algorithmic biases and data privacy. Even while it concentrates on the advantages, such as higher conversion rates and happy customers.The paper addresses the moral dilemmas raised by highly customised advertising and looks ahead to new developments like reinforcement learning and natural language processing. Last but not least, this paper offers great study on how ML techniques have altered personalised marketing, which can assist companies in adjusting to the ever-changing landscape of engagement with consumers.

articleTitle: Cervical Cancer Risk Prediction using SMOTE and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Cervical cancer, accounting for 7.9% of cancers in women globally, is a critical health challenge, particularly due to its asymptomatic nature in early stages. This study proposes a machine learning-driven framework to predict cervical cancer risk using clinical data, addressing class imbalance through SMOTE and optimizing model performance via GridSearchCV. By evaluating five classifiers—K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Support Vector Classifier, Logistic Regression, and Decision Trees—this research identifies the Decision Tree model as the most robust, achieving superior precision, recall, and accuracy metrics. Additionally, Explainable AI techniques such as SHAP and LIME were employed to enhance interpretability, offering clinicians actionable insights into key risk factors driving predictions. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of machine learning in facilitating early detection and personalized treatment strategies for cervical cancer, thereby advancing its integration into clinical applications.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Mobile Healthcare: Societal Impact, Workforce Adaptation, and Enhanced Predictive Modeling for Diabetes Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: With advancements in artificial intelligence, it is natural for the health industry to focus on IOT devices. AI could promote a paradigm shift in how doctors and patients interact through immediate updates, predictive features, and remote access. The focus of this study is the outreach and employment aspects revolving around AI-enabled health care, with special attention to mHealth solutions. We searched through published data and came across 112 relevant studies identifying keywords such as accessibility, empowerment, and workforce. One of the most interesting findings was the fact that AI targeting mobile applications has the possibility of increasing access to health services by approximately 60 percent for rural areas, as well as increasing the patient cooperative rate by approximately 45%, where a predictive health tracking device has been utilized. We proposed two new measures: the Physical Activity and Nutrition Index (PANI) and Health Status Index (HSI), allowing for better diabetes risk predictions with a 0.82 AUC-ROC and better generalizability than traditional baselines, with an improvement of 12%. When identifying the best available ML models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Bayesian Neural Networks, we found that the hybrid Random Forest + Linear SVC model had the best performance with recall and accuracy of 0.77 and 0.72, respectively. The ability of the model to demonstrate both interpretability and specificity was evident. It was also observed that synthetic data augmentation (SMOTE) increased the recall for minority class predictions by 18% but did not reduce specificity.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study of Case-Based Reasoning in Information Retrieval: An Artificial Intelligence Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Information Retrieval (IR) systems which provide accurate and contextually relevant information to healthcare and law etc. where accuracy is very crucial. Traditional information retrieval methods fundamentally based on keyword matching and statistical models usually difficult to achieve the semantic meaning and contextual nuances of queries. Case-Based Reasoning (CBR), as an artificial intelligence technique, provide advance solutions to enhance IR systems based on a set of past cases through adaptive context-supporting retrieval. By taking advantage of past cases data, CBR allows IR systems to interpret complex context-sensitive queries and offer personalized results. The paper provides an overview of traditional IR models, examines the CBR integration into these systems, and evaluates the impact of CBR on retrieval effectiveness and personalization. And finally, we elaborate on the challenges involved with scaling and adapting cases towards real-time retrieval and provide some future directions for research, including integrating machine learning techniques and hybrid models to enhance the relevance, interpretability, and scalability of CBR-based IR systems.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Threat Detection: Implementing Multi-Layer Security Networks in Cloud Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: AI-driven threat detection has become a vital tool for security maintenance as cloud environments become more and more integrated into digital infrastructures. In order to identify and reduce risks in cloud-based systems, this study investigates the deployment of multi-layer security networks utilising cutting-edge machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models. We created a hybrid training strategy that blends historical and synthetic data for improved relevance in contemporary cloud environments by utilising datasets like KDD Cup 99 and CSECIC-IDS2018 in addition to simulated cloud network interactions. ML models such as Random Forest and Logistic Regression were used to create baseline threat detection, while Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks were used to accomplish deeper pattern recognition. The effectiveness of DL models in proactively protecting cloud infrastructures against changing cyber threats was demonstrated by thorough performance evaluations based on accuracy, precision, recall, F1 Score, and AUC-ROC. These evaluations also demonstrated the models’ better flexibility in dynamic cloud environments.

articleTitle: Revolution of Self-Learning in Education from Traditional Pedagogy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The transition from traditional pedagogy to self-learning represents a significant shift in educational practice, propelled by technological advancements and the evolving needs of learners. This study explores the evolution from ancient Gurukul systems to modern digital learning platforms, incorporating data from student survey responses. The analysis reveals a marked preference for hybrid learning models (62.4%) and the widespread use of online resources among participants (91%). Supported by established learning theories and quantitative analysis, the findings indicate that self-learning enhances critical thinking, adaptability, and lifelong learning competencies. The results suggest a future where technology-integrated, personalised learning complements conventional classroom instruction, fostering more independent and proficient learners.

articleTitle: The Future of Marketing Management in Education: AI Applications and Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Educational marketing management helps higher educational institutions (HEIs) discover student demands and improve competition. Despite the significance of educational marketing, HEI adopt the same corporate techniques regardless of their area. To adhere to the changing context of the digital era, HEI must update and improve their marketing tactics based on emerging consumer trends. This study examines the correlation between revenue growth and psychology. It proposes a hybrid approach that uses deep learning's topology to forecast preferences. Employ a hash technique to accurately market to modern age users by analyzing their conduct, knowledge, and recommending relevant resources. This study's framework outperforms five other algorithms in multifaceted recognition evaluation, with an accuracy of 79.7%, recall percentage of 77.5%, F1 of 0.79, and error readings of approximately 0.19 after epoch iteration. The framework is highly useful. Every user's portrait framework is then generated. Portrait enhancement yielded 7 marketing approaches with impressive results, ranging from 70% to 83%. Additionally, the financial position was good. An smart and effective dynamic planning assistance is offered for HEI by the final framework's acceptable design and outstanding data efficiency.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Biomarker Identification for Early Chronic Kidney Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a major health burden that is becoming more and more of a global concern. Improving patient outcomes requires early identification. The present work focuses on identifying key biomarkers for CKD prediction using machine learning classifiers. Biomarkers such as glomerular filtration rate, hemoglobin, proteinuria and serum creatinine are essential for determining kidney damage and function. A dataset of 400 individuals with 25 variables from the UCI ML repository was analyzed and evaluated using six machine learning classifiers: Decision Tree, Random Forest, KNN, Logistic Regression, XGBoost and AdaBoost. Information gain was used to enhance feature selection and missing values were addressed through data preprocessing. The classifiers were assessed using F1-score, recall, accuracy and precision. Among others, KNN showed exceptional performance with 100% recall and 97.22% accuracy. Random Forest and Decision Tree both achieved 97.22% accuracy, along with 96.30% recall and precision. Hemoglobin vs. serum creatinine, Diabetes vs. Hypertension and Specific Gravity vs. Albumin are examples of relationships between biomarkers that were identified as crucial in diagnosing CKD cases. With all classifiers achieving accuracy rates above 96%, the study concludes that machine learning classifiers provide reliable and effective tools for early CKD diagnosis, facilitating prompt intervention and treatment.

articleTitle: A Novel Transfer Learning-based Efficient-Net for Visual Image Tracking
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This study investigates the use of EfficientNet for human identification in congested environments, leveraging the CIFAR-10 dataset. Compared to traditional models such as ResNet, MobileNetV2, VGG16, and VGG19, EfficientNet demonstrated superior performance. The model’s compound scaling method optimizes depth, width, and resolution, achieving outstanding results with lower computational cost. To improve training efficiency, the Swish activation function was implemented, along with data preprocessing techniques including augmentation, normalization, and scaling. After fine-tuning and adjusting the learning rate, Efficient-Net achieved an accuracy of 98%, surpassing other models in precision, recall, and F1-score. This performance showcases the model’s robustness and resilience. The balanced scaling approach of Efficient-Net and its low computational cost make it an ideal choice for real-time applications in image classification and visual tracking. These findings underscore its effectiveness, marking a significant step forward in the field of visual tracking for human identification in crowded settings.

articleTitle: Optimizing Radio Resource Management in Multi-RAT Wireless Networks Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Wireless networks have transformed to be increasingly sophisticated with new-generation radio access technologies. A multi-RAT environment poses a challenge to the network operator in efficiently allocating radio resources to guarantee that users are provided with a high quality of service. Traditionally, radio resource management has been viewed as a static and tuned process, не able to adapt to changes organic structure environments, leading to inefficient radio connections. In this context, reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising framework for managing radio resources in an efficient manner. RL is a method of AI where a system learns from experience directly through trial and error. It is possible to model the radio resource management problem as a Markov decision process and then apply RL algorithms to learn the optimal resource allocation policy with respect to the network states. In this paper, we show how RL can be used for solving radio resource management optimization problem in a novel way at multi-RAT wireless networks. This is especially useful in situations where network conditions are variable and can change over time, leading to improved overall performance and user experience on the network. Network constraints such as user mobility and interference are also considered in our framework to allow for resource allocation.

articleTitle: Intelligent Control Mechanisms for Renewable Energy Integration Using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The deployment of renewable energy sources (RES) in power systems used to be a major challenge owing to their intermittent and uncertain nature. Therefore, in this paper, the use of ML models as an intelligent control system to improve the operation of RES is studied. We survey different types of ML approaches, covering supervised learning for energy predic- tion, unsupervised learning for clustering demand, reinforcement learning for energy storage management, and deep learning for real time data processing. The intent of these advanced control strategies are to balance and stabilize the grid, harmonize demand response, and augment energy storage. We highlight the use-cases and impacts of ML from real-world cases across various geographies, showing operational gains and peak-demand savings. While these technologies hold great promise, they also face challenges like data privacy, interpretability of models, and availability of high-quality datasets. Moving forward, there is a need to improve transparency of algorithms and to strengthen the collaboration of different stakeholders. Our work paves the way for a systematic and automated approach to renewable energy integration, which can serve as a critical factor to build a reliable and efficient future modern power systems with machine learning.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Fraud Detection in Bitcoin Transactions: An AI Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This research looks into how deep learning methods can be used to find fake Bitcoin transfers. It’s mostly about the unique problems and chances that come with trading in cryptocurrencies and blockchain. Deep learning models are used to look at transaction trends and find oddities that could be signs of fraud. This is because Bitcoin’s open structure makes it harder to use traditional methods of fraud detection. We offer a structure that connects CNNs (convolutional neural networks) and RNNs (recurrent neural networks) so that strange patterns can be found in big sets of blockchain transactions. An AI-driven method aims to improve detection accuracy while lowering false positives by taking on scammers’ complicated and always-changing strategies. Experienced researchers have shown that the model is good at finding strange things, which means it can be used to safely stop theft in Bitcoin networks in real time. It looks like deep learning could make digital money safer and give us data that can be used in bigger blockchain-based money systems.

articleTitle: Cross Parametric Analysis and Neural Networks: An Improved Method for Human Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Whenever a disease is present in the body, it manifests through symptoms such as discomfort, changes in physical parameters, and altered behaviors. These variations are commonly assessed to diagnose specific illnesses. For instance, blood glucose fluctuations are used to detect diabetes, while electrocardiogram changes help identify cardiac issues. However, many disorders are interconnected and can be detected more accurately through a cross-parametric model. For example, monitoring blood glucose changes may aid in the early detection of cancer, as prolonged glucose imbalance weakens the body, lowering immunity and red blood cell count, making the body more susceptible to cancer. Over time, cross-parameter illness detection has been widely studied. This text proposes a system for the cross-analysis of diabetes, heart disease, and cancer. The method first evaluates the relationships between various body parameters across these diseases and then assesses how effectively a neural network classifies diseases based on these interconnections. The results show that this cross-parametric approach improves cancer detection accuracy by 5%, heart disease detection by over 4%, and diabetes detection by over 5% compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Using Convolutional Neural Networks for Image Recognition in IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have grown into a powerful picture identification tool. They are an important part of making Internet of Things (IoT) apps. In this regard, CNNs make it possible to analyse visual data gathered from networked devices, like cameras and sensors, effectively and accurately. With an emphasis on its potential for real-time applications for example smart surveillance, healthcare monitoring, autonomous cars, and industrial automation, this study investigates the incorporation of CNN-based image identification into IoT contexts. We tackle important issues such as the requirement for low-latency processing, energy economy, and computing limitations on edge devices. In order to maximise CNN performance in the resource-constrained IoT ecosystem, strategies like model compression, edge computing, and distributed architectures are covered. The ability to interpret large volumes of visual data is improved by the integration of CNNs with IoT, providing creative solutions for automation and intelligent decision-making across numerous industries.

articleTitle: Leveraging XGBoost for Accurate Brain Stroke Prediction: An Innovative Approach to Data-Driven Healthcare Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Leading cause of death and long-term impairment worldwide, stroke calls for efficient prediction and early intervention plans. Leveraging a dataset comprising important patient characteristics including age, gender, medical history (hypertension and heart disease), lifestyle choices (smoking status), body mass index (BMI), and average glucose levels, this work presents a comprehensive approach to estimating stroke risk using the extreme Gradient Boosting (Boost) classifier. The dataset offers a strong basis for classification since it comprises of several cases labelled as stroke (1) or not stroke (0). The approach consists in data preparation to manage missing values and normalise the dataset, then in hyper parameter tuning with grid search to maximise model output. Among the numerous criteria followed in evaluation of the Boost classifier are accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The excellent 95% accuracy of the classification report reveals how successfully the program identifies individuals in risk. With an F1-score of 0.93, one shows a balanced performance; evaluations of precision and recall show a great competence in properly identifying both stroke and non-stroke cases. This work especially in stroke prediction emphasises the possibilities of machine learning methods in medical situations. The outcomes underline the need of data-driven strategies in enabling quick interventions, hence improving patient outcomes and lowering the incidence of stroke-related death.

articleTitle: Machine Learning For Smart School Selection And Admissions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Selecting the appropriate school for their child is one of the decisions that parents are faced with in life, this process can be stressful and uncertain at times. Thus, machine learning is noted to be a possible solution that can be deployed to enhance and optimize the admissions and school selection process in the current periods. The aim of this research is to explore the framework and applicability of machine learning techniques in view of selective admissions, and smart school selection. In the early stages of our investigation, we suggest a simple to use, web based tool where with the aid of different learning machines, all the parents and guardians will be able to find the appropriate school for their child. To help the clients to select particular schools, the website collects and consolidates various information including, but not limited to the following: season activity involvement, academic performance, geographical preferences, and school ranking. This makes the process of selecting a school to attend easier and also helps parents to make right decisions for their children to attend the best school. The second section of this paper describes the procedures of implementing the machine learning techniques in detail, the overviews of the steps of feature selection, data preprocessing, and model evaluation. We also point out the challenges and ethical concerns of employing machine learning for school choice and the problem of an objective machine over a bias one.

articleTitle: Big Data Clustering Algorithms: Improving Efficiency and Scalability for Massive Data Mining and Pattern Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The emergence of big data has completely changed the way data analysis is done. As a result, there is a pressing need for effective clustering algorithms that can handle large datasets from different fields. Efficiency, scalability, and finding meaningful patterns in enormous data are some of the important difficulties that this research tackles in relation to big data clustering. We thoroughly examine and evaluate a range of clustering algorithms, from more conventional ones like hierarchical and K-Means clustering to more cutting-edge ones like density-based spatial clustering (DBSCAN) and model-based clustering. To further improve the performance and scalability of clustering algorithms, we investigate new methods that make use of distributed computing frameworks like Apache Spark and MapReduce. We offer a thorough assessment of their efficacy in terms of clustering quality, computational efficiency, and resource use by using and evaluating these methods on large-scale datasets. While conventional clustering algorithms may fail miserably when faced with extremely big data sets, our research shows that newer methods that make use of optimization techniques and distributed processing greatly outperform their predecessors. The effect of feature selection and dimensionality reduction techniques on improving clustering results is also shown. By shedding light on how to choose and implement clustering algorithms for effective data mining and pattern identification, this study adds to the continuing endeavors in the domain of big data analytics. Progress in areas like customer segmentation, anomaly detection, and social network analysis can be achieved with the help of adaptive algorithms that can handle large datasets while keeping clustering results accurate and dependable, according to the study.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based AI Solutions for Personal Finance Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Cloud-based AI answers for private finance control are out-of-the-field tools that leverage synthetic intelligence and cloud computing technologies to manage people's money higher. In this article, I have described various solutions with features ranging from budgeting to personalized financial planning and investment suggestions. Utilizing superior system learning algorithms and cloud-based AI solutions can help understand an individual's fiscal information, including expenses, profits, or savings transactions, for generating personalized insights and advice. This lets people learn about their spending habits and make more informed financial choices. Through the power of the cloud, these solutions can securely store and access financial data from multiple devices, which helps individuals, manage their finances on the go easily. It also enables the client to get real-time updates and notifications, which offers him more comprehensive knowledge regarding his existing financial scenario. These offerings also come with more automation features like reminders to pay payments and computerized enough transfers for a price range, keeping customers from spending further effort and time on their funds. They also offer financial advisors, tax planning tools, and wealth management.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Approaches for Stock Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Market value forecasting remains one of the most important yet extremely challenging tasks in economic forecasting due to the randomness and complexity of market information. This study systematically examines and compares the effectiveness of two advanced Machine Learning (ML) techniques: the Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network and the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm. Both were trained and tested based on historical AMD price data, using a 95% training ratio and two months moving window to arrange the input variables. The LSTM model demonstrated its capability to effectively capture temporal dependencies inherent in financial time series, achieving a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 2.37. This indicates a high level of precision in its predictions, particularly for modeling longterm trends. On the other hand, the XGBoost model excelled in computational efficiency, producing predictions with a competitive RMSE comparable to that of LSTM, while also handling missing values seamlessly. Visualization of the predictions further underscored the trade-offs between the two approaches. The LSTM model exhibited superior performance in capturing and modeling long-term market trends, while XGBoost offered significantly faster computation times and robust handling of data irregularities. These findings highlight the practical considerations involved in selecting ML models for financial forecasting, including the balance between accuracy, computational cost, and robustness.

articleTitle: An approach Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS): A Hierarchical Deep Learning Framework for Predicting Employee Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The change from traditional techniques of human resource information management to urban computerization approaches was received with discontent by certain government personnel. Still, in this era of computerized governance, this shift is crucial since it improves the efficiency and effectiveness of human resource tasks. In light of this emerging tendency, the government has developed an HRMIS program specifically for use by government agencies. Human Resource Management Information System (HRMIS) is an integrated e-government service that acts as a public sector database and gives government workers a unified interface to do HR-related tasks. The suggested approach consists of two parts: preprocessing and training the model. Transferring data from an unstructured format to one that machine learning systems can work with is the goal of this phase. Data encoding and cleaning are part of the process, as is principal component analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction. It was the HDL that we used for training the model. We outperform state-of-the-art alternatives like CNN and DNN with our proposed model, which obtains an average accuracy rate of 93.58 percent.

articleTitle: Big Data Analytics for Healthcare Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Big Data Analytics for Healthcare Resource Allocation is the new mantra as it integrates vast amounts of complementary data to allocate healthcare resources efficiently. There is an increasing demand for healthcare services, and resources are in limited supply, so doing something as simple as allocating resources can ensure that care quality remains high. The process includes gathering and organizing large datasets from several resources, including electronic health records, patient demographics, service utilization and detailed analysis to generate meaningful findings. Utilizing advanced statistical and analytical techniques, by definition, amongst others, Big Data Analytics can help you decipher the data to show you patterns in resource utilization (how resources are being used), areas where inefficiencies occur which have gone unnoticed long enough that cause them become ripe for incremental year over year cost savings targets or staff reactions if not corrected as then gain media attention likely) some even assembled through different techniques to predict future needs based on past use cases. The advantages of this are manifold. It will help identify high-risk patients, enhance clinical decision-making, and facilitate evidence-based resource allocation. It can also help quantify how well-existing resource distribution strategies work and influence resource planning. Big Data Analytics for Healthcare Resource Allocation: Better Outcome, Cutting Cost and Effective Utilization of Resources This have the potential to revolutionize healthcare resource allocation and improve national healthcare systems' efficiency and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Smart City Cybersecurity: Leveraging Machine Learning for Advanced Ransomware Detection and Prevention
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Data encryption and extortion schemes are hallmarks of ransomware attacks, which have recently arisen as a major cybersecurity concern. The sophistication and frequency of these attacks are increasing, and conventional detection technologies are finding it harder to keep up. Using sophisticated algorithms to spot unusual or suspicious patterns in system activity, this research lays forth a machine learning-based strategy for ransomware attack detection. The suggested model finds ransomware early, before it can do significant damage, by examining both static and dynamic aspects of file activity, network traffic, and system functions. We investigate the efficacy of numerous ML models, comparing their recall, accuracy, and precision. These models include support vector machines, Random Forest, and XGBoost. The findings show that Machine-learning provides a viable and effective technique for identifying ransomware in real-time. Our Method demonstrate 97.333% highest accuracy that leads to classify in two different classes. Along with future research directions for strengthening machine learning models against ransomware variants, we also address problems relating to availability of data, feature selection, and model generalization.

articleTitle: Quantum Bootstrap in Microcanonical Ensembles: Computational Insights and Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This paper explores the quantum bootstrap method, a promising numerical approach rooted in self-consistency conditions, and its application in microcanonical ensembles. Initially developed in the 1960s and ’70s, the bootstrap technique has found applications in various fields, including quantum mechanics, lattice theory, conformal field theory, and matrix models. While extensively studied in quantum mechanics, this paper introduces a classical correspondence to the quantum bootstrap method, expanding its applicability to microcanonical ensembles. The study incorporates a novel approach, demonstrating stronger constraints by integrating additional information in phase space. Numerical examples, including the double well potential, harmonic oscillator, Coulomb potential, and non-relativistic Toda model, illustrate the method’s effectiveness in resolving unphysical energy regions and improving computational precision. These results highlight its potential as a powerful tool in computational physics and quantum computing.

articleTitle: Preliminary Poultry Disease Identification: A Comparative Analysis of Classifiers Utilizing PCA for Improved Agricultural Health Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Diseases in poultry farms have an immense effect on chicken production, food safety, and national economies. The implementation of real-time monitoring and analysis emphasizing chicken production is becoming more popular due to infectious diseases and the rise of animal welfare problems. Disease identification at an early stage can prevent substantial losses for farmers. Despite this, many factors, including the environment, disease outbreaks, breeding procedures, and efficient management techniques, are required for the good production of chickens. Continuous environment monitoring is crucial for mitigating these factors effectively. In literature surveys, it has been mentioned that using modern digital technologies results in excellent accuracy for real-time monitoring and low-cost solutions for poultry production. The Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have remarkably enhanced animal welfare evaluation and monitoring systems, improving chicken quality and reducing mortality rates. Techniques like image processing, computer vision, machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and robotics show great potential to solve many challenges in poultry farms. This study offers a comparative examination of four machine learning classifiers—Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)—integrated with Principal Component examination (PCA) for the early diagnosis of poultry diseases. Utilizing PCA for dimensionality reduction, each classifier exhibited differing levels of accuracy and efficiency. The research highlights the capacity of machine learning to markedly enhance disease identification and management in chicken farms, providing an economical method for monitoring flock health.

articleTitle: Improving Data Encoding for Enhanced AI Performance in Complex Datasets via Quantum Feature Space Mapping: Harnessing Quantum Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the potential for quantum feature space mapping to be utilized in the enhancement of data encoding approaches for artificial intelligence (AI) systems that are capable of managing complicated datasets. Traditional artificial intelligence models frequently face challenges when confronted with the high-dimensionality and non-linearity of such datasets. This can hinder their performance in areas such as pattern recognition, optimization, and predictive modeling. Quantum computing, which is able to make use of quantum superposition and entanglement, provides a method that is revolutionary in nature by means of quantum feature space mapping. By encoding data into quantum states, this technology enables the construction of feature spaces that are tenfold bigger than those that would be possible in classical conditions. This makes it much simpler to differentiate between intricate patterns that would otherwise be indistinguishable. The purpose of this research is to investigate the application of quantum algorithms, such as Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM) and Variational Quantum Classifiers (VQC), with the intention of enhancing the capacity of artificial intelligence to learn from complex and high-dimensional data. We demonstrate that quantum feature space mapping leads to more efficient and accurate data classification, regression, and clustering tasks by comparing the performance of quantum-enhanced artificial intelligence models to that of their classical counterparts on difficult datasets. Additionally, the research addresses important difficulties, such as the constraints of the quantum hardware that is now available and the requirement for quantum circuits that are scalable. Quantum computing has the potential to improve the performance of artificial intelligence in the management of complicated, high-dimensional data, which may ultimately pave the way for advances in domains such as genetics, finance, and cryptography. This work shows that quantum computing has this potential.

articleTitle: Multiple Disease Prediction from Retinal Images Using Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Retinal imaging serves as an essential tool for the early identification and diagnosis of numerous systemic diseases. This model framework is used for predicting multiple diseases simultaneously using retinal images. The implementation begins with the collection of annotated retinal images, enabling the identification of ailments as glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, including hypertensive retinopathy. Preprocessing techniques are applied to enhance data quality and reduce noise. Feature extraction is conducted using the pretrained VGG16 convolutional neural network (CNNis essential for deep learning model training. Multi-label categorization and multi-task learning are employed to predict multiple diseases concurrently. Strict measures, including as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, including the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), are used to assess the system's performance. Clinical validation also evaluates its efficacy in practical settings. The incorporation of this predictive system into clinical workflows is facilitated by ensuring regulatory compliance and seamless communication with healthcare professionals. Experimental Results show that the suggested VGG16-based system accomplishes an impressive 98.7% accuracy in detecting multiple retinal diseases. The implementation underscores the transformative potential of leveraging advanced deep learning techniques in ophthalmology. Future efforts are focused on enhancing algorithm performance through larger datasets and refining models to further improve diagnostic precision, enabling timely and effective treatment strategies for retinal conditions.

articleTitle: Pervasive AI and IoT in STEAM Education: Advancing Future Learning Through Intelligent Systems and Computational Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) continues to transform various sectors, its integration within education, particularly in STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) education, is gaining momentum. This paper explores how AI can enhance STEAM education for K-12 students, preparing them for a rapidly evolving digital world. A review of current literature demonstrates that AI technologies, including virtual reality, augmented reality, machine learning, and IoT, can revolutionize both teaching and learning by promoting critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills. AI-driven tools like ChatGPT, learning analytics, and chatbots provide personalized learning experiences, making education more interactive and engaging. The paper also highlights AI's role in fostering inclusivity and bridging gender gaps within STEAM, particularly in arts education. Furthermore, the paper examines the challenges of AI integration, such as teacher readiness, trust in technology, and the need for professional development. The findings underscore AI's potential to empower educators and students alike, suggesting a roadmap for AI-enhanced STEAM education aligned with sustainable development goals. This research advocates for incorporating AI literacy in curricula to equip students with essential skills for the future.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology: Reshaping Telemedicine and Telehealth Services for Emergency Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Both consumers and healthcare providers have benefited greatly from the quick development of software-based technology. The dominance of blockchains is impending as the medical care sector moves quickly towards digitization and customization. The development of blockchain provided answers to several problems that had long plagued the healthcare sector. However, not only in healthcare due to its capabilities, blockchain technology has found great success in a variety of industrial fields. The important factors propelling the growth of the healthcare blockchain market are the rise in data breaches, privacy concerns, fake pharmaceuticals, and provided answers to numerous problems that had long plagued the healthcare sector. Although telemedicine had been developing for a while, the covid-19 epidemic gave it the necessary kick. In order to facilitate social isolation, the pandemic made it necessary to expand virtual healthcare and distant therapy. Over the past year, the telemedicine market has experienced rapid expansion. In the current study, the adaptation issues and prospective prospects for blockchain technology in the telehealth and telemedicine sectors are explored.Grounded on a systematic review, we have determined the existing state of the use of blockchain technology in a number of healthcare-related areas, the ideal state that would be achieved, the research gap regarding the usage of blockchain technology in a number of healthcare-related application areas, as well as a number of potential research agendas for future studies.

articleTitle: Evaluating Agricultural Soil GHG Emission Models: A Critical Analysis of Identification and Future Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This study focuses on the increasing global challenge of the need for efficacy assessment of techniques and the critical problem of GHG emissions from agrosystems. It addresses their processes, input variables, and simulation results in different cropping systems to present a comprehensive analysis of four well- known process models: DNDC, DayCent, STICS, and APSIM. These may include model structure, management practices, weather conditions, and the level of data available at the time the simulation was built that influence the model's accuracy in the study. Development of appropriate measurement and reduction tools in agriculture is quite essential because, as the IPCC noted, agriculture plays a vital role in global anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases. This study puts forward an integrated hybrid framework, which includes both process-based models and geospatial techniques to increase the precision of emission assessments over varied agricultural systems. The proposed method showed promising improvement in the scalability and robustness of models to enable effective tailoring of mitigation strategies toward sustainable agricultural practices. This paper aims to enhance model accuracy and applicability by offering a methodology focusing on increasing the model's applicability area, unifying the data analysis, and improving the model's algorithms. This project aims to facilitate sustainable food production methods and climate change adaptation by providing better tools and methods to stakeholders by tackling the problem of identifying and managing soil GHG emissions.

articleTitle: Utilizing Machine Learning Algorithms To Predict Chronic Kidney Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a big issue because it happens over time and it doesn't show symptoms until it’s advanced. The models are produced through the use of various machine learning (ML) techniques such as Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Ada Boost, Extra Tree Classifier and Light Gradient Boosting (LGBM). The training and evaluation dataset was provided by the UCI Machine Learning repository and comprised a huge variety of clinical and laboratory characteristics that are associated with the diagnosis of CKD. Performances of the constructed models are evaluated with traditional measures, as common as F1-score, accuracy, precision and recall. Hyperparameter tuning is also used to improve both model accuracy and it’s performance. The additional results are meant to illustrate how well machine learning algorithms can predict CKD, as hyper parameter tuning the extra tree classifier gave an accuracy of 99.16\%. This research may get the field to earlier CKD prediction to guide intervention and improve patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms for Cloud-Based Educational Games: Engaging Students with Adaptive Learning Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The climate of contemporary instruction is changing because of the fast improvement of instructive methodologies. This review looks at a scope of new instructive innovations, including their purposes, benefits, hardships, and potential to reform regular homeroom settings. The research explores how understudy commitment, learning results, and showing approaches are impacted by innovations as well as man-made brainpower (simulated intelligence), virtual reality, augmented reality (AR), gamification, and versatile learning frameworks. The objective of the ongoing task is to decide the ideal calculation for anticipating homeroom investment from understudies. In this review, we gathered information from virtual learning environment (VLE) utilizing versatile learning and handled it utilizing a scope of information preprocessing strategies, like exception ID, standardization, encoding, and missing worth evacuation. Utilizing a scope of commonsense markers and cross-approval draws near, this paper surveyed various AI (ML) characterization frameworks on our information. The outcomes demonstrate that the CatBoost model outperforms the others in terms of accuracy. When compared to earlier studies, this suggested model performed better in every way.
