According to the paper's results section, the CatBoost model's accuracy was roughly 95.34%, its precision was 97.75%, and its recall was 95.4%. The AISAR model was contrasted with when compared to the AISAR 91% model, our model's precision of 97.75% indicates that our findings are superior.

articleTitle: A Novel Deep Learning Model for Machine Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: By seeing early indications of mechanical problems, machinery fault detection helps maintain industrial equipment, cut downtime, and avoid failures. This paper presents a hybrid model that combines AutoEncoders, bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and convolution neural networks (CNN). It achieves a high accuracy of 93%, outperforming traditional methods. The suggested approach uses each component’s advantages to efficiently extract temporal and spatial characteristics from vibration signals that are utilized to diagnose faults. First, a CNN is used to extract local spatial features from the numerical data, which makes it possible to identify patterns linked to different kinds of faults. Following the input of these characteristics, a BiLSTM layer processes the feature sequences in both directions, identifying temporal linkages and long-term dependencies that aid in the understanding of complicated fault patterns over time. An AutoEncoder is used for noise reduction and dimensionality reduction to improve the quality of the features, which improves the representation prior to the final classification step. While regularization methods such as batch normalization and dropout are employed to reduce overfitting, techniques like oversampling and class-weight adjustments are used in the training phase to resolve data imbalance. Grid search is used to adjust hyperparameters in order to maximize model performance. Comparative tests against other architectures, such as ResNet, and VGG, show how successful the hybrid model is as it outperforms them in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. According to the results, the suggested CNN+BiLSTM+AutoEncoder approach offers a reliable and effective way to improve the identification of equipment faults using numerical data.

articleTitle: FedEnv-Net: Federated Neural Network for Decentralized Health Risk Prediction in Dynamic Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The predictions of health risks in urban settings are constrained by factors such as pollution and temperature which change over time. Centralized models have problems with privacy and scalability that often do not allow implementing solutions in real-world large, and distributed systems. To this end, we introduce the FedEnv-Net which is a federated neural network to predict health risk in a decentralized manner. Using federated learning, FedEnv-Net train’s models directly on edge devices, where data is trained and only updates are shared. Dynamics of temporal patterns and features are predicted by LSTM branch and Dense branch respectively in the model. A Meta-Learner merges such branches for prediction and a tuned loss function for conservative health risk estimations. Although it ensures privacy of data, FedEnv-Net yields an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.92 and an MAE of 0.14, which determines its predictive capability. Future work includes increasing the efficiency of the communication between the system components, broadening the number of input data sources and improving the level of privacy to make FedEnv-Net a versatile, privacy-preserving solution for real-time health risk assessment.

articleTitle: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in Insurance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) makes human-machine interactions more transparent and understandable. Given its access to vast amounts of private policyholder data and its critical role in promoting innovation and societal growth, the insurance sector has a great opportunity to demonstrate the capabilities of XAI. The present state of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in insurance practices and research is examined in this article, with an emphasis on their explainability. Through a thorough analysis of 419 primary research papers from 2000 to 2021 from a variety of scholarly sources, the study finds 103 publications that provide an overview of the state of XAI in insurance literature. Using an analysis and classification of these papers, it highlights the use of XAI approaches in critical insurance operations such as claims management, underwriting, and actuarial pricing, among others. In the insurance industry, the study highlights information distillation and rule extraction as the main XAI methodologies. It also promotes the development of interpretable XAI models. By breaking down complex structures into simpler, rule-based ones, this method makes it easier to design models that are easier to understand. By incorporating moral values, openness, and confidence into system design, XAI is a substantial breakthrough in AI. Stakeholders including industry practitioners, regulators, and XAI developers can gain important insights by evaluating these emphasis points within the insurance sector and determining whether regions are ready for more development. By analyzing its applications in the insurance industry, this study provides a fresh viewpoint in addition to enhancing the multidisciplinary understanding of applied XAI. Furthermore, by offering a more nuanced definition based on a thorough analysis of XAI literature within the insurance sector, it adds to the continuing conversations about a precise definition of XAI.

articleTitle: ReIoT-Powered Smart Agriculture in Controlled Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is crucial in improving the agricultural sector. To achieve sustainability and sustained production an innovative approach should be planned, tested, implemented, and proposed to achieve the targeted goals parameters such as pollution, lack of water, and drastic climate changes should be analyzed. This study provides information on how to alleviate these problems, and as a result attain the proposed controlled environment with good-quality air, water, and climate is needed. If these goals cannot be achieved globally, alternate solutions must be set to match current climatic conditions and which crops can sustain unaltered weather patterns and disasters. An in-depth analysis is needed to fine-tune these areas. One application of IoT is the development of a system called "Plants for Survival" (P4S) which aims to solve outdoor problems through detailed studies in a controlled environment. This case study helps predict climatic changes and develops appropriate solutions in a prototype setup. The Data-Driven Development Methodology for IoT-based Systems guides P4S, with quality checks and surveys to ensure efficiency and effectiveness Technology and Parameters that influence weather conditions should be considered while testing in a simulated environment.

articleTitle: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Networks For Stock Market Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks have garnered interest for their ability to remember temporal relations in sequential input. This research employs LSTM networks to estimate prices, which is crucial for stock market predictions. First, we explain the basic concepts of LSTM networks, then we demonstrate how they may be used for time series forecasting by analyzing and interpreting sequential data. Thus, the study begins with a brief overview of LSTM architecture and its potential advantages over traditional models. They show how important feature engineering and data preparation are for stock market prediction using LSTMs. We also consider optimizing LSTM modeling assessment methodologies and hyper parameters. LSTM networks are used in single-step and multi-step stock market forecasting, according to this publication. We employ fundamental research on news emotions and economic indexes to examine how environmental influences affect model efficiency. We also suggest ways to reduce overfitting and data scarcity, which are LSTM's drawbacks for stock market prediction.

articleTitle: Exploring the Use of Machine Learning in Formative Assessment of English Speaking Skills
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The comprehension of English speaking skills is one of the major activities of language acquisition as it gives feedback to learners. Some of the disadvantages of conventional assessment techniques such as scoring and rules base systems are non-extensibility, non-precise and immediate response rate inadequacy. Basic automated solutions of speech recognition do not reflect the sequence of speech and are not very useful in evaluating pronunciation, fluency and intonation patterns. In response to these challenges, this study presents a new CRNN model for formative assessment of speaking skills in English. The proposed CRNN utilizes CNN’s ability of capturing precise details of the spectrograms, and RNN for assessing temporal characteristics of learners’ data, allowing assessment of learning in full. The proposed method encompasses data pre-processing, feature extraction, sequence analysis and real-time formative feedback generation. Al presented experimental outcomes that support the fact that than traditional machine learning techniques, the proposed model gives higher accuracy in assessment of the key speaking skills. Moreover, using the CRNN model, students get individual immediate feedback, which contributes to the better learning. This work will help to complete the work of creating general and automatic means of language diagnostics, which will ensure the presentation of a qualitatively new level of improving the communicative competence of students in the English language.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Model Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks for Online Transaction Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Financial fraud detection is a major challenge faced by financial institutions. For transaction fraud detection, Deep learning and machine learning algorithms are frequently used; however, their efficacy is severely limited by the issue of class imbalance, particularly with regard to the minority fraud class. A thorough study on literature has been done through this research for the examination of the techniques used to handle problems like class imbalance. This work analysed various works on usage of classical machine learning algorithms for transaction fraud detection on unbalanced and balanced datasets produced by under and over sampling. Works on Graph Neural Network that can capture relationships among entities in a graph constructed from the credit card transaction data has also been examined. Furthermore, this work proposes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based approach combined with Adaptive Synthetic Sampling to address the class imbalance problem. The effectiveness has been demonstrated through our preliminary results on AUC, accuracy and other metrics of the approach proposed in learning from the data that is imbalanced as evaluated and compared against other classifiers like Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbour. The proposed approach achieves an accuracy of 97.5% for fraud detection, outperforming other learners. This study provides insights on leveraging Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques to address data imbalance for improved fraud detection performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Network Resilience with Dynamic Traffic Engineering using Load Balancing Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Network resilience has become an important issue given the growing complexity and interdependence of present-day communication networks, as well as their exposure to failures and disruptions. Dynamic Traffic Engineering (DTE) has emerged as a potential solution to improve the resilience of networks through efficient resource usage, increasing network performance and avoiding potential failures. Here, we propose a new power mechanism for enhancing the strength of the network using DTE with a load-balancing mechanism. Load balancing is a tree construction used to distribute traffic across multiple paths to prevent network congestion and reduce network failure probability, which is common in server clusters. However, to do this safely, we need to have our DTE with a balancing approach that does not rely on static route configuration. In this approach, we dynamically redirect traffic at run-time according to network conditions (link failure, congestion, and bandwidth utilization) and ensure optimal resource utilization while avoiding a single point of failure.

articleTitle: ADHERENT-Net: An Adaptive Health Risk Estimation Network for Real-Time Environmental Tracking
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Air borne pollutants greatly affect people’s well-being, so more accurate predictions are essential for the assessment of urban risks. Adaptive Health Risk Estimation Network is proposed in this paper as ADHERENT-Net to predict immediate health risks from environmental data. The model uses LSTM networks for temporal patterns discovery and Dense Neural Network for general feature learning and an additional meta-learner that combines both branches for an enhanced prediction capability. This one is prevented by a particular choice of its loss function where underestimations of threats to health are punished severely enough to prompt timely actions. ADHERENT-Net has a good predictive accuracy: the coefficient of determination, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, is equal to 0,90 and the mean absolute error (MAE) is equal to 0,15. The dual branch structure is capable of handling time-dependent and non-time-dependent data from each other and the meta-learner also increases flexibility in changing conditions such as air quality, and seasonality. Training employed miscellaneous environmental data set with the pre-processing of data completeness and normalized data. ADHERENT-Net creates a reliable foundation for real-time health risk prediction, which has substantial potential to enhance the efficiency of program interventions in urban areas. Future work will concern tuning of the elaborated model parameters, the validation in various scenarios, and the generalization of the framework in other healthcare settings.

articleTitle: Explainable AI for Cardiovascular Health: A SHAP-Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: In this paper an enhanced heart disease risk prediction system using binary classification with Explainable AI(XAI)based framework is proposed. With the initial data preprocessing and EDA, feature engineering is carried out to enhance the predictability of a given data set. The proposed model is trained using Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Random forest where XGBoost outperforms with an accuracy of 85 to 87 percentage and hence used for further development. Ensuring the model is actually making interpretable predictions, the (Shapley Additive Explanations) SHAP algorithm allows a more refined, visual form of feature contribution is implemented. A number of visualizations including interactive plots using Plotly and 3D scatter graphs helps to analyze the relationships between the features that helps to analyse contribution of each feature in SHAP algorithm to visualise using waterfall technique make to understand easily. In the final step, the model is deployed into an interactive, user-friendly Streamlit application built upon joblib and hence an actual tool may be used by people to assess their risk for heart disease.

articleTitle: A Comparative analysis of Network Modelling Approaches for Predicting Performance in Large Scale Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: choosing the right node to measure is the key to success in large-scale networks; network modeling is a critical tool for detecting performance. The growing size and complexity of modern networks make accurately predicting their performance a crucial requirement for efficient and reliable operation. Numerous network modeling approaches, however, each with unique strengths and limitations, have emerged in response to this. This paper provides a comparative critique of these network modeling approaches and their performance prediction capabilities in large-scale networks. The first category is the analytical modeling approach, where mathematical equations represent network performance. An approach similar to the described process gives very accurate and detailed predictions but must rely on a theoretical understanding of how networks behave and the assumption of ideal networks. The second approach, simulation modeling, designs a virtual model of the network and lets you test it to predict its performance. This allows for greater flexibility, and real-world factors can be included in the heuristics; however, it is potentially very computationally intensive. The third method is machine learning, which involves algorithms that learn patterns in historical network data and create predictions. While this method is able to process intricate data sets and adjust to evolving network states, its precision relies heavily on the quality of the training data.

articleTitle: Ethics in Natural Language Processing: Addressing Bias, Privacy, and Misinformation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) stands at the forefront of artificial intelligence, empowering machines with human-like capabilities to process text and speech. The versatile applications of NLP encompass information retrieval, text summarization, text categorization, and machine translation. In the dynamic landscape of information dissemination, the prevalence of misinformation, bias and the need for credible sources have become critical concerns. This research effort addresses critical ethical considerations related to the development of NLP algorithms using the Value Sensitive Design (VSD) framework. This paper explores the intersections between NLP and knowledge graphs, through the lens of VSD aiming to enhance the ethics of NLP solutions.

articleTitle: Machine Vision Technique with Image Segmentation in Digital Diagnostic System for Lung Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Within the domain of medical diagnostics, the integration of machine vision strategies holds guarantee for upgrading precision and effectiveness in disease discovery. Lung cancer remains a critical worldwide wellbeing concern, requiring progressed imaging advances for early and precise conclusion. This paper presents an advanced symptomatic framework enabled by machine vision, especially centring on image segmentation techniques. Through a comprehensive survey of existing writing, we investigate the scene of image segmentation procedures connected to lung cancer location. Hence, we propose a novel system leveraging state-of-the-art machine vision calculations to segment lung images successfully. Our framework points to move forward upon current symptomatic hones by robotizing the division prepare, subsequently encouraging more precise and opportune distinguishing proof of cancerous districts. We examine the potential suggestions of this approach in clinical settings, including its capacity to help radiologists in elucidation and decision-making. Besides, we highlight avenues for future investigate and advancement to refine and optimize the proposed framework for broader clinical selection.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Diagnosis Multi-model System using Late Fuison and Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Lung Cancer and brain tumors are the well-known causes of cancer deaths universal. Therefore, appropriate and accurate diagnosis is an important issue that affects better and more reliable treatment and the patient's chance of survival. Present diagnostic strategies are mostly based on a single piece of information. This often leads to missing necessary information, which can lead to Misidentification of condition or delay in timely treatment. This study presents a novel Computer-Aided-Diagnosis system designed to enhance the detection of lung cancer and brain tumors by integrating multimodal data, including medical images (CT and MRI scans) and clinical information. The proposed approach employs late fusion and ensemble learning techniques, utilizing CNN for processing CT images, VGG19 for analyzing MRI scans, and Random Forest classifiers for evaluating clinical data. By separately training these models, the system capitalizes on the distinct characteristics of each data modality, overcoming the limitations of traditional CAD systems that typically rely on a single data source. This comprehensive analysis not only improves diagnostic accuracy but also provides reliable predictions, ultimately facilitating better clinical decision-making for lung cancer and brain tumor detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Underwater Image Captioning Using Transformer Models and Augmented Terrestrial Datasets
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Underwater environments present unique challenges for image analysis due to light attenuation, scattering, and color distortion, which significantly degrade image quality. These facts make simple operations such as image captioning, which is crucial in marine sciences, search, and conservation, challenging. Current datasets such as Flickr8K contain mostly terrestrial images and do not possess features distinctive to underwater environments therefore direct training of models is not possible in this context. To cover this gap, the current work combines a Transformer-based image captioning model with an enhanced underwater-specific image augmentation set. These augmentations mimic real-life underwater consequences such as RGB attenuation, Gaussian blur, muddy particles, noise, and gradient-based illumination distortions. The implemented model, learned and recursively tuned on the Flickr8k dataset, proves the ability to generate reasonable captions for underwater images even though the dataset belongs to Flickr8k providing a terrestrial environment. This is proven by the enhanced BLEU scores as well as from the results of the experiment which trained the translation model in less than ten percent of the dataset to show its flexibility on underwater scenarios but without necessitating the use of an underwater dataset.

articleTitle: IoT-Driven Data Analytics: Transforming Digital Marketing Campaigns with Real-Time Consumer Insights
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Digital advertising or marketing is being reformed by the Internet of Things (IoT), which makes it conceivable to assemble constant shopper information. Wearable innovation and smart home machines are only two instances of the IoT gadgets that give a large number of conditional, logical, and conduct information. Using IoT-driven investigation of information, advertisers might further develop crusade focusing on, customization, and execution assessment by acquiring commonsense experiences. This paper takes a gander at how IoT data examination might be used into cutting edge promoting, as well as the difficulties and entryways it presents. It similarly covers new subjects including moral issues, man-made brainpower coordination, and insightful assessment, offering an aide for enterprises to really benefit by this perspective change. The developing advertising procedures, for example, all-knowing, shrewd, and logical showcasing, can be easily upheld by this structure. In any case, this thought can likewise benefit from the techniques and procedures for making dependable and secure IoT frameworks, which will help the security and validity of advanced advertising environments in view of IoT.

articleTitle: Integrating Research on AI-Driven Hyper-Personalization: A Review and Framework for Scalable Social Media Campaigns
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework for AI-driven hyper-personalization in social media marketing, addressing the critical gap in existing research that overlooks the integration of technological, strategic, and ethical dimensions at scale. The framework uniquely combines advanced user profiling, dynamic content personalization, and iterative feedback loops to optimize engagement, loyalty, and ROI. It further tackles scalability challenges through innovations like cloud computing and federated learning, while embedding ethical principles of fairness, transparency, and privacy into its design. Unlike prior studies, this paper provides a holistic roadmap for implementing scalable, cross-platform AI systems and explores the integration of emerging technologies such as AR, VR, and blockchain. By synthesizing actionable insights and proposing future research directions, it redefines the potential of hyper-personalized, user-centric marketing strategies in the digital era.

articleTitle: Adaptive Learning Systems: Integrating IoT Sensors with Machine Learning for Dynamic Curriculum Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The broad implementation of learning statistics in different curriculum contexts is still difficult, despite encouraging results in universities. Secondary and primary institutions are hesitant to employ these technologies. By providing individualized education encounters catered to each student's requirements, machine learning (ML) based adaptive learning platforms have revolutionized learning by increasing student involvement and results. Physical training can now be communicated through technology via the growth of the Internet of Things (IoT), which links affordable, diverse gadgets and sensors to open, public spaces. This research investigates the relationship between curriculum adjustment, a crucial aspect of sports, and physical activities using a decision tree. This platform gathers vital statistics from IoT-based wearable sensors, and by virtualization of the gadget, it interacts with the statistics in real time. Implementing and promoting physical education and learning curriculum in the real world and building healthier atmosphere platforms to address the health surveillance problems brought on by IoT sensors are the solutions suggested by the empirical evaluation. Research results demonstrate the remarkable physical activity surveillance accomplished by the suggested approach in comparison to the traditional technologies. With excellent accuracy ratios (98.5%), estimation ratios (96.6%), communication ratios (94.5%), functioning ratios (95.3%), effectiveness ratios (93.4), F-values (92.3%), and lower error rates (17.6%), the computational evaluation of physical education curriculum can assist learners and enhance the related facets of their physical skills.

articleTitle: An Integrated Approach to Network Security: Combining Cryptography and Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: Computer network security is essential to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information stored in computer networks. Cybersecurity now needed to focus on products that went beyond cryptography to protect networks and systems. It can be extended as required by the network and offers a new mechanism for organizations to adopt. It consolidates both processes into one unified security strategy, leveraging the best of both worlds. Cryptography uses mathematical algorithms to keep data safe when it's being sent and stored so that only those with permission can read it. An IDS (Intrusion Detection System) helps identify unusual or suspicious activity in a system's network traffic that indicates a potential cyber-attack.

articleTitle: Machine and Deep Learning Classifications for IoT-Enabled Healthcare Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming academic research and will impact various industries, including healthcare. IoT has transformed healthcare from blast-shaped outdated centralized methods to decentralized smart devices. This led to tailored health systems. Recent advances in wearables, sensor networks, and computing cloud have made large-scale health care IoT usage easier. Despite its serious limitations, IoT can change medicine. Maintenance of various appliances, pricing increases, and the need for greater storage space all issues. IoT is a diverse and durable technology, thus this study will analyze its health sector use. How machine learning and deep learning interact is being studied. The Internet of Things (IoT) health system architecture is also covered in this article, along with its benefits and use cases. This helps highlight IoHT difficulties and encourages academics to create innovative solutions. This paper examines the current work of numerous researchers in machine learning and deep learning, which are heavily linked with IoT-based healthcare approaches.

articleTitle: AI-based Learning Techniques for Bladder Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: There is no doubt that the main issue to address in these patients is the early diagnosis of Bladder carcinoma. This work aims at initiating a new path in this research and undertakes advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning to enhance bladder cancer diagnosis. Bladder cancer is one of the more widespread malignant neoplasms, it is more prevalent in the male population and particularly in male gerontocracy. Conventional diagnostic approaches are hypertrophied and crippled by constraints that lead to diagnostic imperfections and unkind lateness. There stands a great opportunity to deal with these challenges through the implementation of Artificial Intelligence in healthcare. By incorporating the modern artificial intelligence models such as CNN and RNN along with other modern techniques, this research intends to improve the diagnostic outcomes and provide strong prognosis. It is through a comprehensive method of data preprocessing and feature engineering, an incorporation of ethical factors, and the use of complex algorithms that this research hopes to advance the future of precision medicine. In this context, the customized solutions based on the most effective data also expand the scope of the diagnosis of bladder cancer and bring positive changes to the treatment of patients.

articleTitle: Examining Acceptance of AI-Driven Robo-Advisors in the Gulf: An Adapted TAM Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This study examines the factors influencing retail traders’ acceptance of robo-advisors and AI-driven financial tools using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) framework. With the proliferation of digital trading platforms, understanding the determinants that drive or hinder the adoption of robo-advisory services is essential for improving user engagement and trading efficacy. Drawing from a quantitative research design, this study surveyed retail traders to analyze the impact of perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and other TAM-based constructs on traders’ behavioural intentions and actual use of robo-advisors. Statistical analyses, including Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), were conducted to test the hypothesized relationships within the TAM framework. The findings reveal that perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness significantly influence retail traders’ acceptance of robo-advisors, with credibility & trust, perceived behavioural benefits, and perceived user experience emerging as moderating variables. These insights contribute to the growing body of research on financial technology adoption and suggest that enhancing the user experience and addressing perceived gaps could increase adoption rates among retail traders. The study underscores the potential of robo-advisors to support informed decision-making, paving the way for more inclusive financial markets.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Smart Parking with License Plate Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Pervasive Computational Technologies (ICPCT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Smart Parking System that automates the processes of number plate recognition, parking space allocation, and vehicle detection. Utilizing state-of-the-art sensors and image processing techniques, the system aims to improve parking management efficiency. The system continuously tracks vehicles, including cars, bikes, and other types, in real time and monitors available parking spaces, indicating those available for new vehicles. A core feature is Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR), which records and stores vehicle plate numbers upon entry, logging the data in a central database and tracking the vehicle until its exit. This system enhances both the user experience and operational efficiency by reducing the need for manual intervention, improving the accuracy of vehicle identification, and integrating data seamlessly for more effective parking management.
